2.1.10.22: —twenty-one thousand and six hundred are declared the measure of a day and night, O best of gods. ॥22॥
2.1.10.23: Six exhalations and inhalations make one pala; a ghaṭī is said to be sixty palas, and sixty of those make a day and night. ॥23॥
2.1.10.24: But of the inhalations and exhalations arising from Sadāśiva there is no counting; therefore he is held to be imperishable. ॥24॥
2.1.10.25: By my command you must preserve this form for that long, and for that long the work of creation must be carried out through the various guṇas. ॥25॥
2.1.10.26: Brahmā said: Having heard these words of Śambhu, Lord Hari, the self-controlled, together with me, bowed to the Lord of the universe and spoke very softly. ॥26॥
2.1.10.27: Viṣṇu said: O Śaṅkara, ocean of compassion, Lord of the world, please hear this: I shall do all this, following the authority of your command. ॥27॥
2.1.10.28: You will always be the object of my meditation, and never otherwise. All my power was obtained by me from you long ago. ॥28॥
2.1.10.29: O Master, may supreme meditation on you never depart far from my mind even for a moment. ॥29॥
2.1.10.30: And, O Master, whoever, being my devotee, reviles you—grant him, surely and without fail, a dwelling in hell. ॥30॥
2.1.10.31: O Master, whoever is your devotee is indeed dearer to me. For one who understands this, liberation is not hard to attain. ॥31॥
2.1.10.32: My greatness has surely been increased by you today. If ever some fault arises in me, may it be forgiven. ॥32॥
2.1.10.33: Brahmā said: Then Śambhu, having heard his excellent words, said to Viṣṇu with great affection: Your fault will be forgiven by me. ॥33॥
2.1.10.34: Having spoken thus, the Supreme Lord, the treasury of compassion, out of compassion touched both of us, Hari and me, on all our limbs with his hands. ॥34॥
2.1.10.35: Having taught various dharmas, Hara, the remover of all sorrows, gave us two many boons, wishing our welfare. ॥35॥
2.1.10.36: Then the Lord Śambhu, compassionate and loving to his devotees, quickly vanished right there while we two looked on with our eyes. ॥36॥
2.1.10.37: From then on, the rite of liṅga worship has been established in this world. Śambhu, established in the liṅga, bestows enjoyment and liberation. ॥37॥
2.1.10.38: The pedestal of the liṅga is the Great Goddess, and the liṅga is Maheśvara himself. It is called liṅga because of dissolution (layana), for in it the whole universe dissolves. ॥38॥
2.1.10.39: Whoever daily recites the narrative of the liṅga in the presence of a liṅga becomes of Śiva's form within six months; there should be no doubt about this. ॥39॥
2.1.10.40: And whoever performs any act at all near a liṅga—I cannot describe the fruit of his merit, O great sage. ॥40॥
2.1.10.iti: Thus ends the tenth adhyāya, named The supreme truth of Śiva, in the account of creation, in the first khaṇḍa of the second saṃhitā, the Rudra-saṃhitā, of the Śrī Śivamahāpurāṇa. ॥10॥
2.1.11.1: The sages said: O Sūta, O Sūta, most fortunate one, disciple of Vyāsa, salutation to you. Today you have made us hear the wondrous, supremely purifying story of Śiva. ॥1॥
2.1.11.2: In it we heard the wondrous, most divine and auspicious account of the origin of the liṅga, by hearing whose power the destruction of sorrow would come about here in this world. ॥2॥
2.1.11.3: O treasure of compassion, following the dialogue of Brahmā and Nārada, tell us the method of worshipping Śiva, by which Śiva becomes pleased. ॥3॥
2.1.11.4: Śiva is worshipped by brāhmaṇas, kṣatriyas, vaiśyas or śūdras; how should that worship be performed? Tell it as you heard it from the mouth of Vyāsa. ॥4॥
2.1.11.5: Having heard their words, which brought welfare and accorded with the Veda, he spoke everything with affection, in keeping with the sages' questions. ॥5॥
2.1.11.6: Sūta said: Well have you asked about that secret, O lords among sages. I shall tell it today according to my understanding and as I have heard it. ॥6॥
2.1.11.7: Just as it is asked by you, so it was formerly asked by Vyāsa of Sanatkumāra; and that was heard by Upamanyu. ॥7॥
2.1.11.8: Then whatever concerns the worship of Śiva and so on, having been heard by Vyāsa, was taught to me by him out of desire for the welfare of the worlds. ॥8॥
2.1.11.9: That was also heard by Kṛṣṇa from the great-souled Upamanyu. I shall tell it as Brahmā spoke it of old. ॥9॥
2.1.11.10: Brahmā said: Listen, Nārada, I shall describe the worship of the liṅga in brief; O sage, it cannot be told in detail even in a hundred years. ॥10॥
2.1.11.11: Thus one should worship, with supreme devotion, the form of Śaṅkara, blissful, pure and eternal, to obtain the fruit of all desires. ॥11॥
2.1.11.12: Poverty, the suffering of disease, affliction arising from enemies, and the fourfold sin persist only so long as one does not worship Śiva. ॥12॥
2.1.11.13: When the god Śiva is fully worshipped, all sorrow dissolves, every happiness comes about, and afterwards liberation is attained. ॥13॥
2.1.11.14: Whoever, having attained human birth, seeks the chief happiness that comes from progeny, by him Mahādeva, the accomplisher of all undertakings and aims, should be worshipped. ॥14॥
2.1.11.15: Brāhmaṇas, kṣatriyas, vaiśyas and śūdras should perform the worship of Śaṅkara according to rule and in due order, for the fulfilment of all desires and aims. ॥15॥
2.1.11.16: Rising in the early morning, in the period called Brāhma-muhūrta, one should remember the guru and then also Śambhu. ॥16॥
2.1.11.17: Having remembered the holy places and meditated on Hari too, and likewise on me, on the gods, and on the sages and others, O sage, ॥17॥
2.1.11.18: then one should take up a hymn and the names of Śambhu according to rule. Then, getting up, one should void excrement in the southern direction. ॥18॥
2.1.11.19: One should perform the rite of evacuation in a secluded place, as has been taught; that very thing I now describe—listen with attentive mind, O sage. ॥19॥
2.1.11.20: For purification a brāhmaṇa should apply pure earth five times; a kṣatriya four times, and a vaiśya likewise three times. ॥20॥
2.1.11.21: A śūdra should take earth twice for ritual purity—this at the anus; and on the genital organ once, a single time, with care. ॥21॥
2.1.11.22: Ten times on the left hand, seven times on both hands, dear one, on each foot three times, and again three times on the hands. ॥22॥
2.1.11.23: Women should perform the excellent taking of earth as a śūdra does. Having washed the hands and feet, one should take earth as before. ॥23॥
2.1.11.24: Then a man should use a tooth-stick according to the order of his own varṇa. ॥24॥
2.1.11.25: A brāhmaṇa should use a tooth-stick twelve finger-breadths in measure; a king, eleven finger-breadths; a vaiśya should use one of ten finger-breadths. ॥25॥
2.1.11.26: A śūdra should use one of nine finger-breadths—this is the measure laid down in tradition. Considering faults of time, one should avoid a stick defective in measure. ॥26॥
2.1.11.27: The sixth, the first and the new-moon days, the ninth, a vow-day, sunset, Sunday, and likewise the day of a śrāddha, dear one, are forbidden for cleaning the teeth. ॥27॥
2.1.11.28: Bathing should be done according to rule, in due order, at holy waters and the like; according to the particulars of place and time, the bath should be done with mantras. ॥28॥
2.1.11.29: Having first sipped water there, one should put on washed garments; then, staying in a secluded, pleasant spot, one should perform the rite of sandhyā. ॥29॥
2.1.11.30: Having performed the rite as is fitting, one should then begin the procedure of worship, making the mind quite steady and entering the worship-room. ॥30॥
2.1.11.31: Taking up the requisites of worship and sitting on one's own seat, one should first perform nyāsa and the rest, and then worship Hara in due order. ॥31॥
2.1.11.32: First, having duly worshipped the lord of the gaṇas, the door-keepers and likewise the guardians of the directions, one should afterwards arrange the seat of the deity. ॥32॥
2.1.11.33: Or else, having made an eight-petalled lotus, with the articles of worship close by, one should sit there and seat the Lord Śiva upon it. ॥33॥
2.1.11.34: Having sipped water three times and washed the hands again, and having done three prāṇāyāmas, one should meditate on the Three-eyed One in the centre. ॥34॥
2.1.11.35: He is five-faced, ten-armed, resembling pure crystal, adorned with all ornaments, with a tiger-skin as his upper garment. ॥35॥
2.1.11.36: Contemplating one's identity of form with him, a man should always burn away sin. Then, having raised up Śiva in meditation, one should worship the Supreme Lord. ॥36॥
2.1.11.37: Then, having performed purification of the body, one should place the root-mantra on the limbs in order, and everywhere perform the six-limbed nyāsa with the praṇava alone. ॥37॥
2.1.11.38: Having made the application in the heart, one should then begin the worship, and arrange vessels for water for the feet, arghya and ācamana. ॥38॥
2.1.11.39: The wise one should set up nine jars of various kinds according to rule, covering them with darbha grass, placing them on darbha and sprinkling them with water. ॥39॥
2.1.11.40: Into each and every one of them he should pour very cool water; and the intelligent one, examining the substances, should put them into them with the praṇava. ॥40॥
2.1.11.41: He should place vetiver (uśīra) and sandal in the foot-water (pādya). Jasmine, kaṅkola, camphor, banyan root and tamāla — ॥41॥
2.1.11.42: having powdered these properly, he should put them into the water for sipping (ācamanīya). He should have this, mixed with sandal, placed in all the vessels. ॥42॥
2.1.11.43: On both sides of the God of gods he should worship Nandīśa. With perfumes, incense and various lamps he should worship Śiva. ॥43॥
2.1.11.44: Then, having purified the liṅga, the man, filled with joy, should proceed as is fitting with a multitude of mantras beginning with the praṇava and ending with namaḥ. ॥44॥
2.1.11.45: he should conceive the seat — svastika, lotus and the like — with the praṇava. From it, the eastern petal is the imperishable power consisting of aṇimā itself; ॥45॥
2.1.11.46: laghimā is the southern, mahimā likewise the western, prāpti the northern petal, and prākāmya the petal of Pāvaka (south-east); ॥46॥
2.1.11.47: īśitva is the south-western petal, vaśitva in the region of Vāyu (north-west), and sarvajñatva likewise the north-eastern; the pericarp is said to be Soma (the moon). ॥47॥
2.1.11.48: Below the moon is the sun, and below it this fire; below that too he should conceive, in order, Dharma and the rest for Bhava's seat. ॥48॥
2.1.11.49: He should conceive Avyakta and the rest in the four directions, and the three guṇas at the edge of the moon. Having invoked the Supreme Lord with sadyojātaṃ prapadyāmi, ॥49॥
2.1.11.50: with the Vāmadeva mantra he should make him stay upon the seat; with the Rudra-gāyatrī secure his presence, and with the Aghora mantra he should fix him there. ॥50॥
2.1.11.51: He should worship with the mantra īśānaḥ sarvavidyānām. Having offered water for the feet and for sipping, he should present the arghya. ॥51॥
2.1.11.52: He should duly bathe Rudra with water mixed with perfume and sandal, and, according to the rule of the pañcagavya, having consecrated it with mantras in a household vessel, ॥52॥
2.1.11.53: with the praṇava alone he should bathe him with cow's milk, with curd, with honey, and with sugarcane juice, ॥53॥
2.1.11.54: and likewise with ghee, bathing the Worshipful One who brings the welfare of all desires; with holy substances he should anoint Mahādeva with the praṇava. ॥54॥
2.1.11.55: Then he should pour water with mantras into the pure water-vessels. Having purified it properly with a white cloth, the practitioner — ॥55॥
2.1.11.56: should not put it away until he has applied the sandal. Then there he should joyfully worship Śaṅkara with beautiful rice grains, ॥56॥
2.1.11.57: with kuśa, apāmārga, camphor, jasmine, campaka and pāṭala, with white karavīra, with mallikā, lotuses and water-lilies, ॥57॥
2.1.11.58: with various rare flowers, and likewise with sandal and the rest. With water he should arrange a stream of water upon the Supreme Lord. ॥58॥
2.1.11.59: With various vessels he should bathe the god Maheśvara. Worship, which grants all fruits, should be performed preceded by mantras. ॥59॥
2.1.11.60: Those mantras, dear one, for the accomplishment of all desires and aims, I shall tell you briefly; listen attentively. ॥60॥
2.1.11.61: With the Pavamāna mantra, and with the Vāṅmaya, with the Rudra, the Nīlarudra, the auspicious Suśukla, ॥61॥
2.1.11.62: with the Hotāra, likewise the Śīrṣa, the auspicious Atharvaṇa, the Śānti and again the Śānti, with the Bhāruṇḍa and the Aruṇa, ॥62॥
2.1.11.63: with the Arthābhīṣṭa sāman and likewise with the Devavrata, ॥63॥
2.1.11.64: with the Rathantara, the Puṣpa hymn and the Puruṣa hymn, with the Mṛtyuñjaya mantra and likewise with the Five-syllabled mantra — ॥64॥
2.1.11.65: the streams of water should be made a thousand times or a hundred and one, in the Vedic manner, or else with the divine names. ॥65॥
2.1.11.66: Then sandal, flowers and the rest should be placed upon Śiva; likewise with the praṇava he should offer mouth-perfume and the like. ॥66॥
2.1.11.67: Then the god resembling crystal, partless, imperishable, the cause of all worlds, consisting of all worlds, supreme, ॥67॥
2.1.11.68: beyond the reach even of the gods Brahmā, Indra, Upendra, Viṣṇu and others — indeed declared by the knowers of the Veda in the Vedānta to be beyond perception, ॥68॥
2.1.11.69: without beginning, middle or end, the medicine for all the sick, renowned as the Śiva-principle — this Śivaliṅga established there, ॥69॥
2.1.11.70: he should worship on the top of the liṅga with the praṇava mantra alone, with incense, lamps, food-offerings and beautiful betel, ॥70॥
2.1.11.71: then with a lovely waving of lights (nīrājana) according to the prescribed rule, with salutations, hymns and other mantras of various kinds. ॥71॥
2.1.11.72: Having offered arghya, scattered flowers at his feet and bowed down to the Lord of gods, he should worship Śiva with his whole self. ॥72॥
2.1.11.73: Taking flowers in hand, rising up with joined palms, he should again entreat Īśāna, Śaṅkara, with this mantra: ॥73॥
2.1.11.74: Whether out of ignorance or knowingly, whatever japa, worship and the like has been done by me, may it bear fruit by your grace, O Śaṅkara. ॥74॥
2.1.11.75: Having recited thus, he should joyfully place the flowers on Śiva. Then, having performed the svastyayana rite and likewise various blessings, ॥75॥
2.1.11.76: then the sprinkling (mārjana) should again be done over Śiva; then salutation, the asking of forgiveness, and the request for his coming again. ॥76॥
2.1.11.77: Uttering the Aghora mantra, he should make salutation, and there he should pray again with all his heart: ॥77॥
2.1.11.78: Devotion to Śiva, devotion to Śiva, devotion to Śiva, birth after birth. There is no other refuge; you alone are my refuge. ॥78॥
2.1.11.79: Having thus entreated the Lord of gods, the bestower of all accomplishments, he should worship him with supreme devotion, especially with sounds from the throat. ॥79॥
2.1.11.80: Then, having made salutation together with his family and attendants, and having gained incomparable delight, he may go about his work at ease. ॥80॥
2.1.11.81: Whoever, wholly devoted to Śiva, worships him daily in this way, for him indeed every accomplishment arises at every step. ॥81॥
2.1.11.82: He becomes eloquent, and the fruit desired by his mind is certain. Disease, suffering, grief, and likewise anxiety and artificial afflictions such as sorcery, ॥82॥
2.1.11.83: crookedness of others and poison too—whatever suffering has arisen, that suffering Śiva, the supreme bestower of auspiciousness, surely destroys. ॥83॥
2.1.11.84: Welfare arises for him like the moon in the bright fortnight; through the worship of Śaṅkara, good qualities surely grow in him. ॥84॥
2.1.11.85: Thus the method of worship of Śambhu has been told to you, O best of sages. Eager to hear further, what will you ask next, O Nārada? ॥85॥
2.1.11.iti: Thus ends the eleventh adhyāya, named The procedure for worshipping Śiva, in the account of creation, in the first khaṇḍa of the second saṃhitā, the Rudra-saṃhitā, of the Śrī Śivamahāpurāṇa. ॥11॥
2.1.12.1: Nārada said: O Brahmā, O Prajāpati, dear father, blessed are you, whose mind is fixed on Śiva. Tell me this very matter again, properly and in detail, O Creator. ॥1॥
2.1.12.2: Brahmā said: Once, dear son, I, the lotus-born, summoned the sages and the gods from every quarter and spoke good words to them with affection. ॥2॥
2.1.12.3: If you have faith in eternal happiness, if you are desirous of spiritual success, you must come with me to the shore of the ocean of milk. ॥3॥
2.1.12.4: Hearing these words, they went with me to where Lord Viṣṇu, the benefactor of all, dwells. ॥4॥
2.1.12.5: Having gone there, O sage, the gods bowed to Janārdana, the lord of the world, the god of gods, and stood before him with palms properly joined. ॥5॥
2.1.12.6: Then Viṣṇu, seeing those immortals, Brahmā and the rest, standing there, and remembering the lotus feet of Śiva, spoke excellent words. ॥6॥
2.1.12.7: Viṣṇu said: For what purpose have you come, you gods and sages headed by Brahmā? Tell me everything with affection: what task is there now? ॥7॥
2.1.12.8: Brahmā said: Thus questioned then by Viṣṇu as to what task there was now, the gods, together with me, bowing to him again with affection, spoke auspicious words in order to make their purpose known. ॥8॥
2.1.12.9: The gods said: Whose service, removing sorrow, should be performed constantly? ॥9॥
2.1.12.10: Hearing these words, the Lord, affectionate to his devotees, spoke with love and compassion to me along with the gods. ॥10॥
2.1.12.11: The Lord said: O Brahmā, listen. This was properly heard before by you and the gods; nevertheless it is told again to you and likewise to the gods. ॥11॥
2.1.12.12: It has been seen and is seen even today; why then is it asked again now, O Brahmā, by all the gods, who are so often intent on their own aims? ॥12॥
2.1.12.13: The god Śaṅkara, destroyer of all sorrows, is to be worshipped—always worshipped. This was told by him to me, and especially to Brahmā as well. ॥13॥
2.1.12.14: And the whole wondrous example at hand has been seen by you. His worship should never at any time be abandoned by those who desire happiness. ॥14॥
2.1.12.15: Having abandoned Maheśvara, lord of the god of gods, who has the liṅga as his form, these sons of Tāraka likewise perished, together with their kin. ॥15॥
2.1.12.16: They were deluded by me and, through māyā, set far away from Śiva; when they were bereft of Śiva, all were destroyed and ruined. ॥16॥
2.1.12.17: Therefore Hara, who bears the form of the liṅga, is always to be worshipped, and especially to be served with faith, O best of gods. ॥17॥
2.1.12.18: It is through worship of Śarva's liṅga alone that gods and daityas became eminent, and likewise I and you, O Brahmā. How has that been forgotten by you? ॥18॥
2.1.12.19: One should worship that liṅga daily, for whatever reason. Therefore, O Brahmā, Śarva should be worshipped by the gods in the desire for the fruit of all wishes. ॥19॥
2.1.12.20: That is loss, that is a great flaw, that is blindness and that is folly—any moment or even an instant in which one does not worship Śiva. ॥20॥
2.1.12.21: Those devoted to Bhava, whose minds bow to Bhava, and who remember Bhava, are not vessels of sorrow. ॥21॥
2.1.12.22: Delightful houses, women with delightful ornaments, wealth to full satisfaction, a line of sons, grandsons and so on, ॥22॥
2.1.12.23: health and a sound body, and extraordinary renown—those fortunate ones who desire these, or happiness, or the abode of the gods, ॥23॥
2.1.12.24: and at the end the fruit of liberation, or devotion to the Supreme Lord—they, owing to an abundance of past merit, worship Sadāśiva. ॥24॥
2.1.12.25: Whoever, wholly devoted, worships the Śiva-liṅga daily — his attainment is fruitful indeed, and he is not touched by sins. ॥25॥
2.1.12.26: Brahmā said: Thus addressed, the gods then bowed to Hari himself and requested liṅgas for the attainment of all the desires of men. ॥26॥
2.1.12.27: Hearing that, Viṣṇu then addressed Viśvakarman—and so did I, O tiger among sages—intent on the uplift of living beings. ॥27॥
2.1.12.28: O Viśvakarman, fashion auspicious liṅgas of Śambhu in due manner, and they are to be given to all the gods at my command. ॥28॥
2.1.12.29: Brahmā said: Having thus fashioned liṅgas according to each one's entitlement, Viśvakarman gave them to them at the command of me, or of Hari. ॥29॥
2.1.12.30: That I now relate; listen, O best of sages. Śakra worships a liṅga made of ruby; the son of Viśravas (Kubera) a golden one; ॥30॥
2.1.12.31: Dharma a yellow one made of gems; Varuṇa a dark Śiva-liṅga; Viṣṇu one made of sapphire; and Brahmā likewise one made of gold; ॥31॥
2.1.12.32: the Viśvedevas a silver one, and the Vasus likewise; the Aśvins one made of brass or of earth, O sage; ॥32॥
2.1.12.33: the goddess Lakṣmī a crystal one; the Ādityas one made of copper; King Soma a pearl one; Vibhāvasu (Agni) a diamond liṅga; ॥33॥
2.1.12.34: the foremost brahmins and likewise the brahmins' wives an earthen one; Maya one of sandalwood; the Nāgas, with reverence, one made of coral; ॥34॥
2.1.12.35: the goddess one made of butter; the yogī likewise one of ash; the Yakṣas a liṅga of curd; Chāyā likewise one of flour; ॥35॥
2.1.12.36: Brahmāṇī surely worships a jewelled Śiva-liṅga; Bāṇa worships one of mercury, and others an earthen one. ॥36॥
2.1.12.37: Such liṅgas were given by Viśvakarman; all the gods and the hosts of sages worship them. ॥37॥
2.1.12.38: Having given the liṅgas to the gods out of a wish for their welfare, Viṣṇu explained to me, Brahmā, the method of worship of the Pināka-bearer (Śiva). ॥38॥
2.1.12.39: Having heard his words, I, Brahmā, together with the best of gods, came to my own abode, my mind brimming with joy. ॥39॥
2.1.12.40: Having come there, O sage, I properly explained to all the sages and gods the procedure of Śiva's worship, which grants every desire. ॥40॥
2.1.12.41: Brahmā said: Listen, all you sages together with the gods, intent on love: I shall gladly tell the procedure of Śiva's worship, which grants enjoyment and liberation. ॥41॥
2.1.12.42: Having obtained human birth, which is rare among all creatures, and even then birth in a good family, which is hard to obtain, O gods, O lords of sages— ॥42॥
2.1.12.43: —and birth without bodily defect among brāhmaṇas of good conduct, through merit—one should perform the duty prescribed for oneself for the sake of pleasing Śiva. ॥43॥
2.1.12.44: Whatever duty is prescribed for one's caste, that duty one should not transgress. As far as one's means for giving extend, so far should one carry out rites. ॥44॥
2.1.12.45: The sacrifice of austerity surpasses thousands of ritual sacrifices; the sacrifice of japa surpasses thousands of sacrifices of austerity. ॥45॥
2.1.12.46: There is nothing higher than the sacrifice of meditation; meditation is the means to knowledge, since through meditation the yogin sees his chosen deity as of one essence with himself. ॥46॥
2.1.12.47: To one devoted to the sacrifice of meditation Śiva is always near. For those possessing realised knowledge there is no purification by expiation and the like. ॥47॥
2.1.12.48: And those people, O Brahman, who are purified by knowledge and know Brahman—for them there is indeed no ritual action, and, on reflection, no pleasure or pain. ॥48॥
2.1.12.49: Nor merit and demerit, japa, oblation, meditation, or the rule of meditation; through that knowledge, O immortals, they are ever free from change. ॥49॥
2.1.12.50: The liṅga that produces supreme bliss—pure, auspicious, imperishable, partless, all-pervading—should be known as abiding in the hearts of yogins. ॥50॥
2.1.12.51: The liṅga is said to be twofold, O twice-born: external and internal. The external is declared gross; the internal is held to be subtle. ॥51॥
2.1.12.52: Those devoted to ritual sacrifice are devoted to worship of the gross liṅga; for the contemplation of the unrefined, gross forms serve in place of the subtle. ॥52॥
2.1.12.53: He for whom the spiritual (inner) liṅga is not directly perceptible should conceive it in that gross liṅga, and not otherwise. ॥53॥
2.1.12.54: For the wise the subtle, stainless, imperishable liṅga is directly perceived through inner contemplation, just as for the undisciplined the gross liṅga is fashioned from excellent materials and the like. ॥54॥
2.1.12.55: Ah! For one who speaks the truth of reality, on reflection there is nothing else: partless or with parts, in the mind the whole world is pervaded by Śiva. ॥55॥
2.1.12.56: Thus for those liberated through knowledge there is no imputation of fault; nor is there any injunction, nor distinction of enjoined and forbidden. ॥56॥
2.1.12.57: Just as a lotus in water is not stained by the water, so the wise man, though living in a household, is not bound by action. ॥57॥
2.1.12.58: As long as such knowledge has not arisen in a man, so long should a man worship the god Śiva through ritual action. ॥58॥
2.1.12.59: And as an illustration for the worlds: the sun, though stationed in one place and one only, is seen manifold in things such as vessels of water. ॥59॥
2.1.12.60: Whatever in the world is seen or heard, whether of the nature of being or non-being, know all that, O gods, to be the supreme Brahman whose nature is Śiva. ॥60॥
2.1.12.61: The difference among the suns in the waters in this world is due to lack of discernment about the reflection; so say others too, all who have grasped the essential meaning of the Veda. ॥61॥
2.1.12.62: In the heart of the embodied being is the Supreme Lord himself, in full form — for one endowed with such realisation, what use are images and the like? ॥62॥
2.1.12.63: For one lacking such realisation, the conception of an image is beneficial; it is considered a support for a person to climb to the lofty state. ॥63॥
2.1.12.64: Without a support, the lofty state is very hard for him to reach. For men, the support of an image is declared for attaining the attributeless. ॥64॥
2.1.12.65: It is quite certain that attainment of the attributeless comes from worship of the qualified. Thus the image of every god brings conviction. ॥65॥
2.1.12.66: This god is indeed most great, and this worship is for his sake; but why offer perfume, sandal, flowers and the like without an image? ॥66॥
2.1.12.67: The image should be worshipped until realised knowledge arises. If, in the absence of knowledge, one does not worship, his fall is certain. ॥67॥
2.1.12.68: For this reason, O brāhmaṇas, hear the highest truth: whatever duty is prescribed for one's own caste must be performed with effort. ॥68॥
2.1.12.69: Wherever and in whatever way one's devotion lies, worship and the like should be performed; without worship, charity and so on, sin is not far away. ॥69॥
2.1.12.70: As long as sin remains in the body, success does not arise; when his sin is gone, everything becomes fruitful. ॥70॥
2.1.12.71: Likewise, on a dirty cloth dye does not look fine; but when it has been washed and is clean, every dye takes hold. ॥71॥
2.1.12.72: So too, when the body is made pure through proper worship of the gods, the dye of knowledge arises, and then realisation comes about. ॥72॥
2.1.12.73: The true root of realisation is unwavering devotion; devotion alone is also declared the true root of knowledge. ॥73॥
2.1.12.74: The root of devotion is good action—worship of one's chosen deity and the like; its root is said to be a true guru, and his root is the company of the good. ॥74॥
2.1.12.75: Through good company a guru is obtained; from the guru come mantra, worship and the like; from worship devotion arises, and from devotion knowledge is born. ॥75॥
2.1.12.76: From knowledge arises realisation, which illumines the supreme Brahman; and when realisation has arisen, then difference ceases. ॥76॥
2.1.12.77: When all difference has ceased, there is freedom from the suffering of the pairs of opposites; and one free from that suffering becomes of the form of Śiva. ॥77॥
2.1.12.78: When the opposites are no longer encountered, pleasure and pain do not arise for the knower; nor, O divine sages, do enjoined and forbidden exist for him. ॥78॥
2.1.12.79: Such a person, free from the householder's life, is rare in the world; if one exists in this world, he removes sin by his mere sight. ॥79॥
2.1.12.80: Here the holy places praise such a foremost knower of true knowledge, and so do the gods and all the sages, regarding him as Śiva, whose nature is the supreme Brahman. ॥80॥
2.1.12.81: The holy places are not like that, nor are the gods made of clay and stone; they purify after a long time, whereas the man of realised knowledge purifies even by being seen. ॥81॥
2.1.12.82: As long as one remains in the householder stage, so long should one, with great love, perform worship of a form—of the best among the five gods. ॥82॥
2.1.12.83: Or else Śiva should be worshipped; the one root is pre-eminent. When the root is watered, the branches are satisfied; likewise, it being so, all the gods are satisfied. ॥83॥
2.1.12.84: But when the branches are well satisfied, the root is never satisfied. In the same way, O best of sages, when all the gods are satisfied, ॥84॥
2.1.12.85: Śiva's satisfaction is by no means to be understood as following by those of subtle intellect. But when Śiva is worshipped, all the gods are indeed worshipped. ॥85॥
2.1.12.86: Therefore, devoted to the welfare of all beings, one should worship the god Śaṅkara, the benefactor of the world, for attaining the fruits of all desires. ॥86॥
2.1.12.iti: Thus ends the twelfth adhyāya, named The discernment of the essential and the inessential, in the description of the procedure of worship within the account of creation, in the first khaṇḍa of the second saṃhitā, the Rudra-saṃhitā, of the Śrī Śivamahāpurāṇa. ॥12॥
2.1.13.1: Brahmā said: Next I shall describe the unsurpassed procedure of worship. Listen, O sages and gods: it brings the happiness of all desires. ॥1॥
2.1.13.2: Rising at the Brāhma muhūrta, one should remember Śiva together with Ambā, and with devotion, palms joined and head bowed, should offer a prayer to him. ॥2॥
2.1.13.3: Rise, rise, O Lord of gods; rise, O you who dwell in the heart; rise, O Lord of Umā, and bring auspiciousness to the universe. ॥3॥
2.1.13.4: I know dharma, yet I have no inclination toward it; I know adharma, yet I have no turning away from it. O Mahādeva, as I am directed by you who abide in my heart, so I act. ॥4॥
2.1.13.5: Having spoken these words with devotion and remembered the guru's feet, one should go outside toward the south to void feces and urine. ॥5॥
2.1.13.6: Then, having purified the body by cleansing with earth and water and having washed the hands and feet, he should clean his teeth. ॥6॥
2.1.13.7: Before the lord of day (the sun) has risen, having cleaned the teeth, he should then rinse the mouth sixteen times with handfuls of water. ॥7॥
2.1.13.8: O divine sages, the sixth and other such lunar days, the new-moon day, the ninth, and Sunday should be carefully avoided by the devotee for cleaning the teeth. ॥8॥
2.1.13.9: As opportunity allows, one should bathe well in rivers and the like, or at home; a man should take a bath that does not conflict with place and time. ॥9॥
2.1.13.10: On Sunday, likewise at a śrāddha, at a saṅkrānti, at an eclipse, at a great gift, at a tīrtha, and on a day of fasting, ॥10॥
2.1.13.11: or when ritual impurity has come, one should not bathe with hot water. The devout man should bathe at a tīrtha and the like facing the current, as is proper. ॥11॥
2.1.13.12: One may anoint the body with oil after considering the weekdays in order; for daily anointing, scented oil is not faulted. ॥12॥
2.1.13.13: It is to be avoided at a śrāddha, at an eclipse, on a fast, and on the pratipad day; or else mustard oil is not faulted, except at an eclipse. ॥13॥
2.1.13.14: Having thus considered place and time, one should bathe according to rule, facing north or else facing east. ॥14॥
2.1.13.15: He should never bathe in a soiled garment; he should bathe in a clean garment, remembering that deity. ॥15॥
2.1.13.16: A garment worn by another or soiled is not to be used; but that which was worn at night — with it the bath may be done, and after washing it one should set it aside. ॥16॥
2.1.13.17: Then tarpaṇa should be performed, which gives satisfaction to the gods, sages and ancestors. Then a washed garment should be worn, and one should again sip water (ācamana). ॥17॥
2.1.13.18: Then, going to a clean spot wiped with cow-dung and the like, an auspicious seat should be arranged there, O best of the twice-born. ॥18॥
2.1.13.19: The seat should be made of pure wood, whole, or else spread with covering; likewise one may make a variegated seat, which grants the fruit of all desires. ॥19॥
2.1.13.20: Whatever is suitable, such as a deerskin, should also be taken. Seated there, the wise one should make the tripuṇḍra with ash. ॥20॥
2.1.13.21: Japa, austerity and charity become fruitful through the tripuṇḍra. In the absence of ash, water and the like are prescribed there. ॥21॥
2.1.13.22: Having thus made the tripuṇḍra, a man should wear rudrākṣas; and having completed his own duties, he should then worship Śiva. ॥22॥
2.1.13.23: Again performing ācamana three times with mantras — or once — one should say gaṅgābindu (a drop of the Gaṅgā). ॥23॥
2.1.13.24: Likewise he should bring there food and water for Śiva's worship, and whatever other things, according to his means, keeping them near at hand. ॥24॥
2.1.13.25: Having done so, one should remain right there, composed and steady; and likewise prepare one arghya vessel filled with water, fragrance and unbroken rice, ॥25॥
2.1.13.26: and it should be placed at the right shoulder for arranging the offerings. Having remembered the guru and obtained his permission, ॥26॥
2.1.13.27: having duly made the saṅkalpa (resolve) and set forth his desire, he should worship Śiva with his retinue with supreme devotion. ॥27॥
2.1.13.28: Showing one mudrā, he should worship the Remover of obstacles Gaṇeśa, accompanied by Siddhi and Buddhi, with vermilion and other substances. ॥28॥
2.1.13.29: Having worshipped him there together with Lakṣa and Lābha, he should bow again, with name-words in the dative case, ending in namaḥ and beginning with the praṇava (Oṃ). ॥29॥
2.1.13.30: Then, having asked pardon of this god together with his brother, he should worship with supreme devotion and bow again and again. ॥30॥
2.1.13.31: Having worshipped the doorkeeper Mahodara, who always stands at the door, he should afterwards worship the chaste Girijā. ॥31॥
2.1.13.32: Having worshipped Her with sandal paste, saffron, incense, lamps in many ways, and various food offerings, then worshipping Śiva, ॥32॥
2.1.13.33: and bowing again there, he should go into Śiva's presence. If at home, he may fashion an image of earth, or of gold, or of silver, ॥33॥
2.1.13.34: or another made of metal, or one of mercury, he should fashion; bowing again to it, he should worship it, intent on devotion. ॥34॥
2.1.13.35: When that image is worshipped, all deities become worshipped as well. He should also install a liṅga of clay, having made it according to rule. ॥35॥
2.1.13.36: The observances must be followed there in every way by those dwelling in their own homes. Having performed bhūtaśuddhi (purification of the elements), one should perform prāṇapratiṣṭhā (infusing life). ॥36॥
2.1.13.37: In a Śiva temple he should install and worship the guardians of the directions there; at home Śiva is always to be worshipped through the application of the root mantra. ॥37॥
2.1.13.38: There at home, however, there is no rule at all regarding the doorkeepers. In the liṅga that is worshipped at home, everything is established. ॥38॥
2.1.13.39: At the time of worship, having invoked the god with his limbs and together with his retinue, one should worship him; there is no further restriction here. ॥39॥
2.1.13.40: Having come into Śiva's presence, he should arrange his own seat; then, sitting facing north, he should again perform ācamana. ॥40॥
2.1.13.41: After washing the hands, one should perform prāṇāyāma; there itself a man should carry it through ten rounds with the root mantra. ॥41॥
2.1.13.42: The five mudrās, formed with the hand and essential for worship, are to be made; having displayed these mudrās, a man should carry out the rite of worship. ॥42॥
2.1.13.43: Then, having lit a lamp there and then made obeisance to the guru, having assumed there the lotus posture, or else the bhadrāsana, ॥43॥
2.1.13.44: or having adopted the uttānāsana, or likewise the paryaṅkāsana — seated in whatever way is comfortable — and again performing the procedure, ॥44॥
2.1.13.45: having done so, he should clear away the worship offerings made earlier with a vaṭṭaka; or if one worships by oneself here at home, there is no such rule. ॥45॥
2.1.13.46: Afterwards he should wash the excellent liṅga with the arghya vessel, having become single-minded and having set out the materials of worship. ॥46॥
2.1.13.47: Then a man should invoke the god with this mantra: Him who abides on the peak of Kailāsa, the supreme lord of Pārvatī, ॥47॥
2.1.13.48: Śambhu of the form as described, beyond attributes yet having the form of attributes, five-faced, ten-armed, three-eyed, whose emblem is the bull, ॥48॥
2.1.13.49: white as camphor, of divine body, moon-crested, with matted locks, having a tiger-skin as upper garment and an elephant-hide as auspicious clothing, ॥49॥
2.1.13.50: whose body is encircled by Vāsuki and other serpents, equipped with Pināka and other weapons, before whom the eight siddhis dance here without ceasing, ॥50॥
2.1.13.51: served by hosts of devotees with cries of Victory! Victory! — hard to behold because of his unbearable splendour, served by the gods, ॥51॥
2.1.13.52: the refuge of all beings, with a gracious lotus-face, as sung by the Vedas and śāstras, ever praised by Viṣṇu and Brahmā, ॥52॥
2.1.13.53: loving to his devotees, bliss itself — Śiva I invoke. Having thus meditated on Śiva together with Ambā, he should offer a seat. ॥53॥
2.1.13.54: He should do everything in due order with a word ending in the dative; then he should offer water for the feet, and then arghya to Śaṅkara. ॥54॥
2.1.13.55: Then, having offered ācamana to Śambhu, the Supreme Self, he should afterwards joyfully bathe Śaṅkara with the five substances. ॥55॥
2.1.13.56: Then, as appropriate, with Vedic mantras or with names accompanied by mantras, in words ending in the dative, he should devotedly offer the substances. ॥56॥
2.1.13.57: Likewise he should offer upon Śaṅkara whatever substance is desired; and then the water-bath (vāruṇa snāna) is to be given to Śiva. ॥57॥
2.1.13.58: He should carefully offer fragrant sandal-paste and other unguents; and with fragrant water he should arrange a continuous stream of water. ॥58॥
2.1.13.59: With Vedic mantras, or with the six-limbed mantras, or with the names, eleven times (the number of the Rudras), as time allows — having offered it, he should then wipe the liṅga with a cloth. ॥59॥
2.1.13.60: Afterwards he should offer ācamana, then present a garment. Sesame, or barley, wheat, mung and black gram — ॥60॥
2.1.13.61: are thus to be offered to Śiva, with mantras of various kinds. Then flowers are to be given to the five-faced great-souled one, ॥61॥
2.1.13.62: to each face according to its meditation-form and according to suitable desire: with lotuses, hundred-petalled lotuses, conch-flowers and other flowers, ॥62॥
2.1.13.63: with kuśa-flowers, dhattūra, mandāra, droṇa flowers, and likewise with tulasī leaves and especially with bilva leaves, ॥63॥
2.1.13.64: he should worship Śaṅkara, who loves his devotees, with supreme devotion. In the absence of everything else, a bilva leaf is to be offered to Śiva. ॥64॥
2.1.13.65: By the offering of a bilva leaf alone the whole worship is accomplished. Then fragrant powder and excellent scented oil, ॥65॥
2.1.13.66: of various kinds, are to be offered to Śiva with supreme joy. Then incense is to be offered joyfully with guggulu and aguru. ॥66॥
2.1.13.67: Then a lamp steeped in ghee is to be given to that Śaṅkara. Again he should devotedly offer him arghya with this mantra. ॥67॥
2.1.13.68: With feeling and devotion he should wipe the face with a cloth. The mantra: Give beauty, give fame, and give enjoyment, O Śaṅkara; ॥68॥
2.1.13.69: give the fruit of enjoyment and liberation; accepting the arghya — salutation to you. Then various auspicious food-offerings (naivedya) are to be given to Śiva. ॥69॥
2.1.13.70: Then he should lovingly offer ācamana without delay; then, having prepared betel for Śiva with all its ingredients and accompaniments, ॥70॥
2.1.13.71: he should perform the ārati with a five-wicked lamp, counting as follows: four times at the feet, twice at the navel, ॥71॥
2.1.13.72: once at the face, and seven times over the whole body. Then, having meditated as prescribed, he should recite the mantra. ॥72॥
2.1.13.73: A man should carry out the mantra rite according to the prescribed number and according to his knowledge; the wise one, having done the mantra-japa by the method taught by the guru — ॥73॥
2.1.13.74: Having done it by the method taught by the guru, he should recite the mantra; a man should carry out the mantra rite according to the prescribed number and according to his knowledge. ॥74॥
2.1.13.75: With hymns of various kinds he should lovingly praise the bull-bannered one; then he should slowly circumambulate Śiva. ॥75॥
2.1.13.76: Then the man should make prostrations with the eight limbs, according to rule. Then a handful of flowers is to be offered devotedly with this mantra, ॥76॥
2.1.13.77: to Śaṅkara, the supreme lord, for the sake of Śiva's satisfaction: Whatever worship and the like has been done by me, whether in ignorance or with knowledge, ॥77॥
2.1.13.78: may that be fruitful by your grace, O Śaṅkara. I am yours, my life is in you, my mind is ever on you, O Mṛḍa — ॥78॥
2.1.13.79: knowing this, O Lord of Gaurī, O Lord of beings, be gracious to me. For those whose feet have slipped on the ground, the ground itself is the support; ॥79॥
2.1.13.80: for those who have committed offences against you, you alone are the refuge, O Lord. Having made many such entreaties properly, according to the rule, ॥80॥
2.1.13.81: Having offered a handful of flowers, one should again bow down repeatedly and say: O Lord of the gods, O master, go to your own abode together with your retinue. ॥81॥
2.1.13.82: And at the time of worship, O Lord, you should come again with kindly regard. Having thus entreated Śaṅkara, who is affectionate to his devotees, many times, ॥82॥
2.1.13.83: one should dismiss him into one's own heart and place that water on one's head. Thus, O sages, the worship of Śiva, which bestows both enjoyment and liberation, has been told in full. What else do you wish to hear? ॥83॥
2.1.13.iti: Thus ends the thirteenth adhyāya, named The worship of Śiva, in the account of creation, in the first khaṇḍa of the second saṃhitā, the Rudra-saṃhitā, of the Śrī Śivamahāpurāṇa. ॥13॥
2.1.14.1: The sages said: O disciple of Vyāsa, O greatly fortunate one, tell us precisely: worshipped with which flowers does Śambhu bestow which fruit? ॥1॥
2.1.14.2: Sūta said: O sages headed by Śaunaka, listen attentively to all of it: today, with great delight, I shall tell the determination about the offering of flowers. ॥2॥
2.1.14.3: This very procedure was asked of Brahmā by the great sage Nārada; he with supreme delight declared the determination about the offering of flowers. ॥3॥
2.1.14.4: Brahmā said: One who desires prosperity (Lakṣmī) should worship the god Śiva with lotuses, bilva leaves, and also with hundred-petalled lotuses, and likewise with conch-flowers. ॥4॥
2.1.14.5: If Śiva is worshipped with these, numbering a hundred thousand, there is destruction of sins, O brahmin, and there will be prosperity; there is no doubt about this. ॥5॥
2.1.14.6: Twenty lotuses are declared to make one prastha; a thousand bilva leaves are defined as half a prastha. ॥6॥
2.1.14.7: A thousand hundred-petalled lotuses are defined as half a prastha. A prastha is sixteen palas, and a pala is held to be ten ṭaṅkas. ॥7॥
2.1.14.8: When one places the offerings on the scale by this very measure, one obtains all desires; if he is free of desire, he becomes Śiva. ॥8॥
2.1.14.9: He who desires a kingdom should please the god Śaṅkara by the worship of earthen liṅgas, ten crores in number, O lords of sages. ॥9॥
2.1.14.10: The liṅga as Śiva, and flowers, and unbroken rice grains, the liṅga anointed with sandal paste, and also a stream of water, ॥10॥
2.1.14.11: for each liṅga a mantra, and an excellent bilva leaf, or a hundred-petalled lotus, or else a lotus, ॥11॥
2.1.14.12: and likewise with conch-flowers, as specially declared by the ancients — this worship is divine, yielding the fruit of all desires, here and hereafter, in every way. ॥12॥
2.1.14.13: incense, lamp, food-offering, arghya, and also ārati, circumambulation, prostration, and the asking of forgiveness and the dismissal of the deity — ॥13॥
2.1.14.14: he who, having performed all this with its accessories, and likewise has made a feeding of brahmins here — to him Śaṅkara surely grants a kingdom in every way. ॥14॥
2.1.14.15: The man who desires pre-eminence should worship with half of that number; one who is in prison should worship Hara with a lakh. ॥15॥
2.1.14.16: When one is afflicted by disease, he should worship Śiva with half of that; he who desires a maiden as bride should again worship Śiva with half of that. ॥16॥
2.1.14.17: Likewise, one who desires learning should worship Śiva with half of that; one who desires eloquent speech should worship Śiva with ghee. ॥17॥
2.1.14.18: For driving away enemies, the worship is of that same measure; for killing them, with a lakh; and for infatuating, with half of that. ॥18॥
2.1.14.19: For conquering vassal chiefs, worship of a crore is praised; and in the rite of subjugating kings, a worship numbering ten thousand. ॥19॥
2.1.14.20: For fame, and likewise for vehicles and the like, the number is a thousand. One desiring liberation should worship Śambhu with five crores, with true devotion. ॥20॥
2.1.14.21: One seeking knowledge should worship Śaṅkara, the benefactor of the world, with a crore; one desiring a vision of Śiva should worship with half of that. ॥21॥
2.1.14.22: Likewise the Mṛtyuñjaya mantra should be repeated according to the fruit desired; when five lakh repetitions are done, Śiva becomes directly manifest. ॥22॥
2.1.14.23: With one lakh a person comes to worship truly; with the second, a good birth arises; with the third, attainment of desires; with the fourth, he beholds him. ॥23॥
2.1.14.24: And when the fifth lakh is completed, he grants the fruit without doubt. By this same mantra, at ten lakhs, the full fruit comes about. ॥24॥
2.1.14.25: He who desires liberation should perform worship with darbha grass. The number everywhere should be understood as a lakh, O best of sages. ॥25॥
2.1.14.26: He who desires long life should perform worship with dūrvā grass; he who desires a son should perform it with dhattūra flowers. ॥26॥
2.1.14.27: The dhattūra with a red stalk is held to be auspicious in worship. And with agastya flowers, the worshipper gains great fame. ॥27॥
2.1.14.28: If one worships with tulasī, his fruit is enjoyment and liberation; with arka flowers comes splendour, and likewise with kubjaka and kahlāra flowers. ॥28॥
2.1.14.29: Worship with japā (hibiscus) flowers is held to bring death to enemies; karavīra flowers here, in due course, drive away diseases. ॥29॥
2.1.14.30: With bandhūka flowers comes the attainment of ornaments; with jātī (jasmine), one gains vehicles, no doubt. With atasī flowers worshipping the god, one attains the state of being dear to Viṣṇu. ॥30॥
2.1.14.31: Likewise with śamī leaves liberation is attained by a man; when mallikā flowers are offered, Śiva grants a most auspicious wife. ॥31॥
2.1.14.32: With excellent yūthikā flowers, one is never deprived of a home; likewise with karṇikāra flowers, wealth of garments arises for men. ॥32॥
2.1.14.33: With nirguṇḍī flowers, the mind in this world attains purity; likewise with a lakh of bilva leaves, one obtains all desires. ॥33॥
2.1.14.34: With śṛṅgārahāra flowers, one prospers in happiness and wealth; flowers born of the season bestow liberation, no doubt. ॥34॥
2.1.14.35: Rājikā (mustard) flowers here bring death to enemies. One should offer a lakh of these to Śiva, and he would grant abundant fruit. ॥35॥
2.1.14.36: There is no flower that is not dear to Śiva. Leaving aside campaka and ketaka, one may offer everything else. ॥36॥
2.1.14.37: After this, O excellent one, listen with delight to the full measure and fruit of grains in the worship of Śaṅkara. ॥37॥
2.1.14.38: When men offer rice grains upon Śiva, following the rule of unbroken grains and with proper devotion, O brahmin, an increase of prosperity arises. ॥38॥
2.1.14.39: Six prasthas, and again half of that prastha, and two palas — this is declared as the measure of a lakh of rice grains. ॥39॥
2.1.14.40: Having performed the worship chiefly with the Rudra mantra, one should then place a very beautiful cloth over Śiva; the offering of rice there is excellent. ॥40॥
2.1.14.41: On top one should place a single śrīphala, along with fragrance, flowers and the like; having set it there and having offered incense and the rest, the fruit of the worship will arise. ॥41॥
2.1.14.42: Two Prājāpatya fees and a fee counted in silver māṣas should be given to the one who instructed it; or else the fee is considered to be given according to one's capacity. ॥42॥
2.1.14.43: Then one should feed brāhmaṇas there, twelve in number (the number of the Ādityas). Thus the lakh-worship is accomplished, complete with its auxiliaries and preceded by mantras. ॥43॥
2.1.14.44: There the rule for the mantra is declared as one hundred and eight repetitions. A lakh of sesame seeds, measured in palas, destroys the great sins. ॥44॥
2.1.14.45: The measure of a lakh is declared to be just eleven palas. The worship there should be performed as before, out of desire for one's welfare. ॥45॥
2.1.14.46: Therefore brāhmaṇas should be fed here; this must be done by the man. The sorrow born of great sins surely perishes at that very moment. ॥46॥
2.1.14.47: Likewise the worship of Śiva with a lakh of barley grains is declared supreme; its measure is eight prasthas and again half a prastha, ॥47॥
2.1.14.48: together with two palas — this is the ancient measure there. And barley worship is said by the sages to increase the happiness of heaven. ॥48॥
2.1.14.49: And those who desire the fruit should perform a Prājāpatya for the brāhmaṇas. Likewise worship of Śaṅkara with grains of wheat is praised. ॥49॥
2.1.14.50: His progeny increases if it is performed up to a lakh. A lakh would be half a droṇa; the procedure is according to rule. ॥50॥
2.1.14.51: In worship with mung beans, the god Śiva indeed grants happiness; the measure is seven prasthas, or again with half a prastha more, ॥51॥
2.1.14.52: together with two palas — thus the lakh is stated by the ancients. And brāhmaṇas should likewise be fed, to the number of the Rudras (eleven). ॥52॥
2.1.14.53: Just by worship with priyaṅgu of the Supreme Self, the overseer of dharma, dharma, wealth and desire increase; this worship brings every happiness. ॥53॥
2.1.14.54: For it, one lakh is stated by the ancients to be one prastha; and the feeding of brāhmaṇas is likewise declared to the number of the suns (twelve). ॥54॥
2.1.14.55: Worship of Śambhu with black mustard (rājikā) is held to bring about the enemy's death; likewise a lakh of mustard seeds is measured at twenty palas. ॥55॥
2.1.14.56: And by worship with them the enemy's death is declared. Having adorned the liṅga with leaves of āḍhakī, one should worship Śiva. ॥56॥
2.1.14.57: A chosen cow should be given, and likewise a bull. Worship with black pepper is held to destroy the enemy. ॥57॥
2.1.14.58: Having coloured the liṅga with leaves of āḍhakī, one should worship Śiva; this worship brings various joys and grants every fruit. ॥58॥
2.1.14.59: Thus I have told you the measure of grains, O best of sages; now hear with delight, O lord of sages, the measure of a lakh of flowers. ॥59॥
2.1.14.60: One prastha of śaṅkhapuṣpa flowers is declared to be a lakh by Vyāsa, who shows the subtle measures. ॥60॥
2.1.14.61: The measure of a lakh of jātī jasmine is proclaimed as eleven prasthas; likewise the measure of yūthikā; that of rājikā is half of it. ॥61॥
2.1.14.62: The excellent measure for mallikā is twenty prasthas; likewise the measure for sesame flowers is somewhat less than a prastha. ॥62॥
2.1.14.63: Then for karavīra flowers the measure is held to be threefold that; for nirguṇḍī flowers the measure is stated likewise by the wise. ॥63॥
2.1.14.64: Likewise the measure for karṇikāra, and again for śirīṣa flowers, and the measure for bandhujīva, is ten prasthas. ॥64॥
2.1.14.65: Having considered the measure by these and various other flowers, one should perform the worship of Śiva for the fulfilment of all desires, or, free of desire, for liberation. ॥65॥
2.1.14.66: Next I shall tell the great fruit of stream-worship (dhārā-pūjā), by merely hearing which welfare arises for men. ॥66॥
2.1.14.67: Having performed the worship of Śiva with devotion according to the prescribed procedure, those intent on devotion should afterwards make a stream of water. ॥67॥
2.1.14.68: For allaying fever and delirium a stream of water is auspicious — done with the Śatarudriya mantra, or with the eleven anuvākas of Rudra, ॥68॥
2.1.14.69: or with Rudra-japa there, or with the Puruṣa-sūkta, or with the six-limbed mantra, or with the Mahāmṛtyuñjaya, ॥69॥
2.1.14.70: or with the Gāyatrī, or with names beginning with Oṃ and ending in namaḥ, or with mantras stated in the Āgamas — so too the stream of water and the rest. ॥70॥
2.1.14.71: For the increase of happiness and progeny, stream-worship is excellent, performed lovingly with various auspicious, divine substances by one who wears holy ash. ॥71॥
2.1.14.72: A stream of ghee should be poured on Śiva for as long as a thousand mantras are recited; then the expansion of one's lineage occurs — there is no doubt here. ॥72॥
2.1.14.73: Thus Śiva's worship should be done with ten thousand mantras for allaying the disease prameha, and one would obtain what the mind desires. When impotence has arisen, then excellent worship with ghee is prescribed; and the feeding of brāhmaṇas, a Prājāpatya, is likewise declared by the lords of sages. ॥73॥
2.1.14.74: When one becomes dull of intellect, then especially a stream of milk alone, mixed with sugar, should be made there. ॥74॥
2.1.14.75: For him there arises an excellent intellect like that of Jīva (Bṛhaspati). The stream-worship should go on until ten thousand mantras are complete. ॥75॥
2.1.14.76: And when agitation arises in the body without cause, or when love, wherever it may be, has turned to growing sorrow, ॥76॥
2.1.14.77: and when quarrels constantly arise in one's own house — when that stream is performed, all sorrow dissolves. ॥77॥
2.1.14.78: To torment enemies, a stream of oil should be poured over Śiva with great effort; success in the undertaking will surely come. ॥78॥
2.1.14.79: With scented oil, increase of enjoyments arises; with mustard oil, the destruction of enemies will surely occur. ॥79॥
2.1.14.80: By worshipping Śiva with honey one would indeed become king of the Yakṣas; and a stream of sugarcane juice poured on Śiva also brings every kind of joy. ॥80॥
2.1.14.81: A stream of Gaṅgā water indeed grants the fruit of both worldly enjoyment and liberation. All these streams that have been described are to be accompanied by the Mṛtyuñjaya mantra. ॥81॥
2.1.14.82: In that rite, the recitation should be performed to the count of ten thousand, according to its prescribed procedure; and a meal for brāhmaṇas should be given, to the number of the Rudras eleven. ॥82॥
2.1.14.83: All this that I was asked, O lord of sages, I have told you. This is indeed fruitful in the world and brings the benefit of all desires. ॥83॥
2.1.14.84: What fruit one obtains by worshipping Śambhu together with Skanda and Umā according to the rule, with devotion, that I shall tell as I have heard it. ॥84॥
2.1.14.85: Having enjoyed here every auspicious happiness with sons, grandsons and others, he then goes to the world of Maheśa, which brings every happiness, ॥85॥
2.1.14.86: with aerial chariots shining like ten million suns, moving wherever desired, thronged with Rudra-maidens and filled with song and instrumental music, ॥86॥
2.1.14.87: and, having become like Śiva, he sports there until the dissolution of beings; then, having obtained imperishable knowledge, he attains liberation. ॥87॥
2.1.14.iti: Thus ends the fourteenth adhyāya, named The rules for worshipping Śiva, in the account of creation, in the first khaṇḍa of the second saṃhitā, the Rudra-saṃhitā, of the Śrī Śivamahāpurāṇa. ॥14॥
2.1.15.1: Nārada said: O Vidhi, O Vidhi, most fortunate one, you are blessed, best of gods! Today you have let me hear the wondrous, supremely purifying story of Śiva. ॥1॥
2.1.15.2: In it I heard the wondrous, most divine and auspicious account of the origin of the liṅga; by hearing of its power, sorrow is destroyed here in this world. ॥2॥
2.1.15.3: Now tell me in detail what happened after that, its greatness and the deeds, and also the manner of creation. ॥3॥
2.1.15.4: Brahmā said: You have asked well about what happened after that. I shall tell it briefly, just as I heard it before. ॥4॥
2.1.15.5: When the eternal god in Śiva's form had then vanished, O chief of brahmins, I and Viṣṇu attained great joy. ॥5॥
2.1.15.6: Then the forms of the swan and the boar taken by me and by Viṣṇu were withdrawn by the two of us, with the wish to create and protect the worlds. ॥6॥
2.1.15.7: Nārada said: O Vidhi, O Brahmā, most wise one, there is a great doubt in my heart. Showing incomparable kindness, please dispel it quickly. ॥7॥
2.1.15.8: Why did you two assume the forms of the swan and the boar, setting aside any other form? Tell me the reason for this. ॥8॥
2.1.15.9: Sūta said: Having heard these words of the great-souled Nārada, Brahmā, remembering the lotus-feet of Śiva, spoke respectfully. ॥9॥
2.1.15.10: Brahmā said: The swan's movement in flying upward is steady; and it has the discernment between reality and unreality, like separating water from milk. ॥10॥
2.1.15.11: The swan distinguishes the truth of ignorance and knowledge; therefore the swan form was assumed by that Brahmā, the maker of creation. ॥11॥
2.1.15.12: Yet discernment of the truth of Śiva's own nature, whose form is light, was not attained at all, O Nārada, because the swan faculty failed. ॥12॥
2.1.15.13: How can knowledge of Śiva arise in one who desires to engage in creation? For that reason discernment was not attained by me, even in the swan form. ॥13॥
2.1.15.14: The boar's movement in going downward is steady; therefore the boar form was assumed by Viṣṇu, the forest-roamer. ॥14॥
2.1.15.15: Or else, that form of the boar was devised by Viṣṇu, the protector of the worlds, for the sake of establishing a kalpa of existence. ॥15॥
2.1.15.16: Beginning from the day on which Hari assumed that form, that day marks this kalpa named the Vārāha kalpa. ॥16॥
2.1.15.17: Or, from the day when his wish to assume that form arose, that day marks this kalpa named the Vārāha kalpa. ॥17॥
2.1.15.18: Thus the answer to your question has been given. Now hear the matter at hand, O Nārada: remembering the lotus-feet of Śiva, I shall describe the process of creation, O sage. ॥18॥
2.1.15.19: When Mahādeva had vanished, I, the grandsire of the worlds, intent on meditation, contemplated how to carry out his command. ॥19॥
2.1.15.20: Then, having bowed to Śambhu and having received knowledge from Hari, attaining supreme bliss, I set my mind on creating. ॥20॥
2.1.15.21: Viṣṇu too, then and there, having bowed down to Sadāśiva and having instructed me, dear son, disappeared. ॥21॥
2.1.15.22: Going outside the cosmic egg and having obtained Śambhu's grace, Hari went to the city of Vaikuṇṭha and dwelt there forever. ॥22॥
2.1.15.23: There, with the desire to create, remembering Śiva and Viṣṇu, I scooped up a handful of the water that had been created earlier and cast it forth. ॥23॥
2.1.15.24: From that an egg arose there, called the twenty-four (made of the twenty-four principles). It had the form of Virāṭ, O brahmin, though to me, not discerning it, it appeared as a form of water. ॥24॥
2.1.15.25: Then, overcome by doubt, I practised extremely severe austerity there for twelve years, wholly devoted to meditation on Viṣṇu. ॥25॥
2.1.15.26: At that time, dear son, Hari himself appeared and, joyfully touching my body, spoke to me with great affection. ॥26॥
2.1.15.27: Viṣṇu said: Ask for a boon; I am pleased. There is nothing that cannot be given to you, O Brahmā; by Śambhu's grace I am able to give everything. ॥27॥
2.1.15.28: Brahmā said: This is fitting, O most fortunate one, for I was entrusted to you by Śambhu. What he spoke of, I ask of you today: grant it, O Viṣṇu; salutation to you. ॥28॥
2.1.15.29: This egg, of the form of Virāṭ and called the twenty-four, has no consciousness at the outset; it appears inert. ॥29॥
2.1.15.30: You have appeared today through Śiva's grace, O Hari. Bring consciousness into this egg, which was obtained through Śaṅkara's power. ॥30॥
2.1.15.31: When this was said, Mahāviṣṇu, devoted to Śambhu's command, assumed an infinite form and entered that egg. ॥31॥
2.1.15.32: That Puruṣa with a thousand heads, a thousand eyes and a thousand feet, touching the earth on all sides, pervaded that egg. ॥32॥
2.1.15.33: When Viṣṇu, well praised by me, had entered that egg, the egg called the twenty-four became conscious. ॥33॥
2.1.15.34: Beginning from Pātāla up to the highest, Hari himself, lord of Satyaloka, shone there as the Vairāja Puruṣa, the Lord. ॥34॥
2.1.15.35: The five-faced one Śiva made the lovely city of Kailāsa, shining above all, as a dwelling for himself. ॥35॥
2.1.15.36: Even when the cosmic egg is destroyed, O divine sage, there is never any destruction here of those two, Vaikuṇṭha and that Kailāsa. ॥36॥
2.1.15.37: Having taken my abode in the Satya realm, O best of sages, I remained there; and by Mahādeva's command, dear son, I became desirous of creating. ॥37॥
2.1.15.38: Then, as I wished to create, there first appeared a sinful creation, dear son: the fivefold Avidyā, preceded by intellect, resembling darkness. ॥38॥
2.1.15.39: Then, with a calm mind, I created the principal creation called the immobile beings, and by Śambhu's command I meditated, free of attachment. ॥39॥
2.1.15.40: Seeing that, and judging whether it served my purpose, as I wished to create, there arose a creation full of suffering, the tiryak-srotas (animal creation), which did not serve my purpose. ॥40॥
2.1.15.41: Realising that this creation too was ineffective, and as I was thinking again, a sāttvika creation called Ūrdhvasrotas ('whose stream flows upward') quickly came into being. ॥41॥
2.1.15.42: It is renowned as the creation of the gods, true and bringing exceeding happiness. Considering that too to be ineffective, I meditated on my own Lord. ॥42॥
2.1.15.43: Then, by Śaṅkara's command, a rājasa creation appeared, known as Arvāksrotas ('whose stream flows downward'): the human creation, which accomplishes the highest goal. ॥43॥
2.1.15.44: Then, by Mahādeva's command, the creation of the elements and the rest (bhūtādi) came about. Thus the fivefold creation was set going, made by me. ॥44॥
2.1.15.45: Three creations of Prakṛti and of Brahman are proclaimed. Among them the first is the creation of Mahat, the second is that of the subtle elements, ॥45॥
2.1.15.46: and the third is the vaikārika creation; these are the three prākṛta creations. Thus there are eight kinds of creation, the prākṛta together with the vaikṛta. ॥46॥
2.1.15.47: The Kaumāra is declared the ninth; it is both prākṛta and vaikṛta. The sub-divisions of these cannot be told by me. ॥47॥
2.1.15.48: Because its usefulness is slight, I only speak of the creation consisting of the twice-born: the Kaumāra, in which the great creation of Sanaka and the others took place. ॥48॥
2.1.15.49: Sanaka and the others were indeed my mind-born sons, equal to Brahman, endowed with great dispassion, five of them, firm in their vows. ॥49॥
2.1.15.50: Though commanded by me, those wise ones, turned away from worldly existence, their minds fixed solely on meditation on Śiva, did not set their minds on creation. ॥50॥
2.1.15.51: Hearing the reply given by them, O best of sages, I became exceedingly fierce with anger and fell into delusion, O Nārada. ॥51॥
2.1.15.52: Then, O sage, as I was enraged, deluded and agitated, drops of tears fell from my eyes because of anger. ॥52॥
2.1.15.53: At that moment there, I was awakened to my senses by Viṣṇu, who, remembered by me in my mind, had come swiftly. ॥53॥
2.1.15.54: Instructed by Hari with the words, perform penance directed to Śiva, I performed a great, terrible and supreme penance, O best of sages. ॥54॥
2.1.15.55: As I was performing penance for the sake of creation, from between my eyebrows and nose, in particular from my own region called Avimukta, ॥55॥
2.1.15.56: there appeared the treasury of compassion, the full portion of Maheśa, who is above the three forms, the Lord of all, having become Ardhanārīśvara. ॥56॥
2.1.15.57: Him, the unborn Śaṅkara in person, a mass of radiance, the lord of Umā, all-knowing, the maker of all, called Nīlalohita, ॥57॥
2.1.15.58: having seen, bowed to with great devotion and praised, I, delighted, said to the Lord of the gods of gods: Create diverse beings. ॥58॥
2.1.15.59: Then, hearing my words, that god of gods, Maheśvara, Rudra, created many Rudra-gaṇas equal to himself. ॥59॥
2.1.15.60: I spoke again to the Lord, Mahārudra, Maheśvara: O God, create beings who are subject to the fear of birth and death. ॥60॥
2.1.15.61: Hearing my words thus, Mahādeva, the treasury of compassion, laughed and at once spoke to me, laughing, O best of sages. ॥61॥
2.1.15.62: Mahādeva said: I shall not create beings possessed by the fear of birth and death, O Vidhi (Brahmā), beings that are inauspicious, subject to karma, sunk in the ocean of sorrow. ॥62॥
2.1.15.63: But I, taking on the form of a guru, shall lift up the beings sunk in the ocean of sorrow by bestowing true knowledge. ॥63॥
2.1.15.64: You yourself, O Prajāpati, create all the beings full of sorrow. By my command you will not be bound by Māyā. ॥64॥
2.1.15.65: Brahmā said: Having said this to me, the blessed, most glorious Nīlalohita, Hara, together with his gaṇas, quickly vanished while I looked on. ॥65॥
2.1.15.iti: Thus ends the fifteenth adhyāya, named The appearance of Rudra's avatāra, in the beginning of creation, in the first khaṇḍa of the second saṃhitā, the Rudra-saṃhitā, of the Śrī Śivamahāpurāṇa. ॥15॥
2.1.16.1: Brahmā said: Having quintuplicated by myself the elements beginning with sound, from them I created the gross sky, wind, fire, water and earth, ॥1॥
2.1.16.2: mountains and oceans and trees and so on, O Nārada; and I created the units of time from the kalā up to the yuga, and others as well, ॥2॥
2.1.16.3: and still others up to the completion of creation; yet I was not satisfied, O sage. Then, having meditated on Śiva together with Ambā, I created the sādhakas (spiritual practitioners), O sage. ॥3॥
2.1.16.4: Marīci from my two eyes, Bhṛgu from my heart, Aṅgiras from my head, and Pulaha, best of sages, from the vyāna breath; ॥4॥
2.1.16.5: Pulastya from the udāna breath, Vasiṣṭha from the samāna, Kratu from the apāna, Atri from my two ears, and Dakṣa from the prāṇa breath. ॥5॥
2.1.16.6: Then I created you from my lap, and the sage Kardama from my shadow; from my resolve I created Dharma, the means of all means of attainment. ॥6॥
2.1.16.7: Having thus created these foremost practitioners, I became fulfilled, O tiger among sages, through the grace of Mahādeva. ॥7॥
2.1.16.8: Then, dear one, by my command Dharma, born of my resolve, assumed a human form and was set in motion by the practitioners. ॥8॥
2.1.16.9: Then from the various limbs of my body I created countless sons—gods, demons and others—giving to each of them his respective body, O sage. ॥9॥
2.1.16.10: Then, impelled by Śaṅkara dwelling within me, I divided my own body in two and became of twofold form, O sage. ॥10॥
2.1.16.11: With one half I became a woman and with the other half a man, joined continuously, O sage. He (the man) produced in her a couple, excellent, the means of all accomplishment. ॥11॥
2.1.16.12: There the man was Svāyambhuva Manu, the supreme means of creation; the woman, named Śatarūpā, was a yoginī and an ascetic. ॥12॥
2.1.16.13: She, exceedingly beautiful, was then taken as wife by that Manu according to the rite of marriage, dear one, and he brought forth creation through sexual union. ॥13॥
2.1.16.14: From him in her were born the son Priyavrata, likewise Uttānapāda, and also three daughters. ॥14॥
2.1.16.15: They were renowned as Ākūti, Devahūti and Prasūti. He gave Ākūti to Ruci, and the middle one to Kardama. ॥15॥
2.1.16.16: He gave Prasūti, the daughter younger than Uttānapāda, to Dakṣa. By their offspring and descendants the whole world of moving and unmoving beings was pervaded. ॥16॥
2.1.16.17: From Ruci in Ākūti was born a pair, Yajña and Dakṣiṇā; and to Yajña in Dakṣiṇā twelve sons were born. ॥17॥
2.1.16.18: From Kardama in Devahūti many daughters were born, O sage; and from Dakṣa were born twenty-four daughters. ॥18॥
2.1.16.19: Thirteen of them, beginning with Śraddhā, were given by Dakṣa to Dharma. Hear the names of those wives of Dharma, O lord of sages. ॥19॥
2.1.16.20: Śraddhā, Lakṣmī, Dhṛti, Tuṣṭi, Puṣṭi, Medhā and Kriyā, Buddhi, Lajjā, Vasu, Śānti, Siddhi and Kīrti — these are the thirteen. ॥20॥
2.1.16.21: Remaining after them were eleven younger, fair-eyed ones: Khyāti, Satpathā, Sambhūti, Smṛti, Prīti and Kṣamā, ॥21॥
2.1.16.22: Sannati and Anurūpā, Ūrjā, Svāhā and Svadhā. Bhṛgu, Bhava, Marīci, and likewise the sage Aṅgiras, ॥22॥
2.1.16.23: Pulastya, Pulaha, and Kratu the best of seers, Atri, Vasiṣṭha, Vahni (Fire) and the Pitṛs (Ancestors), in due order— ॥23॥
2.1.16.24: these eminent practitioners, Bhṛgu and the rest, took those renowned maidens as wives. Thereby the entire three worlds with their moving and unmoving beings were filled. ॥24॥
2.1.16.25: Thus, in accordance with the karma of living beings and by the command of Ambikā's lord, many countless excellent twice-born were born. ॥25॥
2.1.16.26: According to a difference of kalpa, Dakṣa is said to have had sixty daughters. Of them he gave ten to Dharma, twenty-seven to the Moon, ॥26॥
2.1.16.27: and Dakṣa duly gave thirteen to Kaśyapa; four he gave to Tārkṣya of excellent form, O Nārada. ॥27॥
2.1.16.28: And he gave two daughters each to Bhṛgu, Aṅgiras and Kṛśāśva. From those daughters and those husbands arose an abundant creation of moving and unmoving beings. ॥28॥
2.1.16.29: The thirteen daughters who were duly given by Dakṣa to that great-souled Kaśyapa, O best of sages— ॥29॥
2.1.16.30: by their offspring the three worlds with moving and unmoving beings were pervaded; nothing, whether stationary or mobile, was left empty. ॥30॥
2.1.16.31: Gods, seers and Daityas were born, and trees, birds, all mountains and creepers. ॥31॥
2.1.16.32: Thus the moving and unmoving world was pervaded by those born of Dakṣa's daughters, surely, from the floor of Pātāla up to Satyaloka. ॥32॥
2.1.16.33: The entire cosmic egg was pervaded and was never empty. Thus creation was properly accomplished by Brahmā at Śambhu's command. ॥33॥
2.1.16.34: She named Satī, ever protected by Rudra on the tip of his trident, was formerly fashioned for the sake of austerity by Śambhu, who is all-pervading. ॥34॥
2.1.16.35: She herself was born from Dakṣa for the sake of the world's purpose, and performed many sports (līlā) in order to uplift the devotees. ॥35॥
2.1.16.36: He whose left side is Vaikuṇṭha (Viṣṇu), whose right side is I myself, and from whose heart Rudra is born—that Śiva is declared to be threefold. ॥36॥
2.1.16.37: I, Viṣṇu and Rudra are declared to be the three guṇas; but Śiva himself is ever beyond the guṇas, the supreme Brahman, imperishable. ॥37॥
2.1.16.38: Viṣṇu is sattva, I am rajas, and Rudra is declared to be tamas—so it is said according to worldly usage and in name; in reality it is otherwise. ॥38॥
2.1.16.39: Viṣṇu is tamas within and sattva without; Rudra likewise is held to be sattva within and tamas without; I am rajas in every way, O sage. ॥39॥
2.1.16.40: The goddess Surā (Sarasvatī) is rājasic; Satī is of the nature of sattva; Lakṣmī is to be known as tāmasic; and the supreme Śivā is of threefold form. ॥40॥
2.1.16.41: Thus Śivā, having become Satī, was married by Śaṅkara. At her father's sacrifice, because of disrespect, she gave up her body and went to her own abode. ॥41॥
2.1.16.42: And again Śivā was born as Pārvatī at the request of the gods; having performed very great austerity, she again attained Śiva. ॥42॥
2.1.16.43: And many names of hers arose, O lord of sages: Kālikā, Caṇḍikā, Bhadrā, Cāmuṇḍā, Vijayā, Jayā, ॥43॥
2.1.16.44: Jayantī, Bhadrakālī, Durgā and Bhagavatī; Kāmākhyā, Kāmadā, Ambā, Mṛḍānī, Sarvamaṅgalā — ॥44॥
2.1.16.45: These and many other names, bestowing enjoyment and liberation, corresponding to her qualities and deeds — among them Pārvatī is the chief one. ॥45॥
2.1.16.46: Likewise the goddesses composed of the guṇas and the three gods composed of the guṇas, uniting together, carried out the excellent and varied work of creation. ॥46॥
2.1.16.47: Thus, O best of sages, the manner of creation has been described to you; the whole cosmic egg was fashioned by me at Śiva's command. ॥47॥
2.1.16.48: Śiva is declared the supreme Brahman; the three gods are his forms — I, Viṣṇu and Rudra — according to the distinction of the guṇas. ॥48॥
2.1.16.49: He sports freely with Śivā in the delightful Śivaloka; the Supreme Self is indeed independent, without attributes and yet also with attributes. ॥49॥
2.1.16.50: Rudra, his complete incarnation, is regarded as Śiva himself directly. The five-faced one made a lovely dwelling on Kailāsa; and even at the destruction of the cosmic egg, there is certainly no destruction of it. ॥50॥
2.1.16.iti: Thus ends the sixteenth adhyāya, named The description of creation, in the dialogue of Brahmā and Nārada within the beginning of creation, in the first khaṇḍa of the second saṃhitā, the Rudra-saṃhitā, of the Śrī Śivamahāpurāṇa. ॥16॥
2.1.17.1: Sūta said: O lords among sages, having heard these words of Brahmā, that Nārada bowed to him and humbly questioned him again. ॥1॥
2.1.17.2: Nārada said: When did Śaṅkara, who is loving towards his devotees, go to Kailāsa? And where did his friendship with the great-souled Kubera come about? ॥2॥
2.1.17.3: What did Hara, the perfect one of auspicious form, do there? Tell me all this; my curiosity is very great. ॥3॥
2.1.17.4: Brahmā said: Listen, Nārada, I shall tell the story of the moon-crested one: how he went to Kailāsa and how he gained the friendship of the giver of wealth. ॥4॥
2.1.17.5: In the city of Kāmpilya there lived an initiated priest named Yajñadatta, born in a family of Soma-sacrificers and expert in the lore of sacrifice. ॥5॥
2.1.17.6: He knew the Vedas and Vedāṅgas, was wise, skilled in Vedānta and the like, honoured by the king, generous in many ways, and a vessel of fame. ॥6॥
2.1.17.7: He was devoted to tending the sacred fire and intent on Vedic study; handsome, of lovely limbs, with a form like the disc of the moon. ॥7॥
2.1.17.8: This initiated priest had a son named Guṇanidhi; having received the sacred thread at eight, he acquired learning abundantly, and then, without his father's knowledge, he became addicted to gambling. ॥8॥
2.1.17.9: Taking money from his mother again and again, he gave it to gamblers and made friends with them. ॥9॥
2.1.17.10: He abandoned Brahmin conduct, turned away from the twilight rites and bathing, reviled the Vedas and scriptures, and reviled gods and Brahmins. ॥10॥
2.1.17.11: Devoid of the conduct enjoined by smṛti, he indulged in the amusements of song and instruments, and was bound in a chain of affection with actors, heretics and jesters. ॥11॥
2.1.17.12: Even when urged by his mother, he did not go near his father. The initiated priest, occupied with other household tasks, would ask his wife— ॥12॥
2.1.17.13: Whenever he would ask her, O auspicious one, my son Guṇanidhi is not seen by me in the house; what is he doing? — ॥13॥
2.1.17.14: then each time she would say: He has just gone out. Having bathed and worshipped the gods, for all this time — ॥14॥
2.1.17.15: having studied, he has gone with two or three friends for further study. Thinking, he is my only son, his mother deceived the priest. ॥15॥
2.1.17.16: The priest knew nothing at all of his deeds or his conduct. Then, in his sixteenth year, he performed for him the complete keśānta (first shaving) rite. ॥16॥
2.1.17.17: Then the priest Yajñadatta had that son of his married according to the procedure laid down in the Gṛhya texts. ॥17॥
2.1.17.18: Every day, O Nārada, his mother, her heart moist with affection, would seat her son Guṇanidhi beside her and gently admonish him: ॥18॥
2.1.17.19: Son, your father, that great soul, is extremely quick to anger. If he learns of your conduct, he will beat both you and me. ॥19॥
2.1.17.20: I constantly hide your misdeeds from your father. Your father is honoured by people for his good conduct, not for wealth. ॥20॥
2.1.17.21: Dear one, the wealth of Brahmins is true learning and the company of the good. Why do you not, with a glad mind, make these your delight? ॥21॥
2.1.17.22: Your forefathers were true śrotriyas, learned in the Veda, initiated priests and Soma-sacrificers; thus they gained renown here. ॥22॥
2.1.17.23: Give up association with the wicked and delight in the company of the good. Set your mind on true learning and practise the conduct of a Brahmin. ॥23॥
2.1.17.24: You resemble your father in appearance, in fame, in family and in character; so why are you not ashamed before us? Give up your wickedness. ॥24॥
2.1.17.25: You are nineteen, and she is sixteen. Cherish this virtuous wife, and be devoted to your father. ॥25॥
2.1.17.26: Your father-in-law too is honoured everywhere for his virtue and character. So why are you not ashamed before us? Give up your wickedness, son. ॥26॥
2.1.17.27: Your maternal uncles, son, are unequalled in learning, character, lineage and the like; yet you do not fear even them. You are pure on both sides of your lineage. ॥27॥
2.1.17.28: Look at these Brahmin boys living in the neighbouring houses; look also at these pupils of your father in our own house, fittingly disciplined. ॥28॥
2.1.17.29: When the king too hears of your misconduct, son, he will lose his regard for your father and cut off his livelihood. ॥29॥
2.1.17.30: Even now people call this mere childish behaviour; later they will take away our rightful status as initiated priests here. ॥30॥
2.1.17.31: Everyone will revile your father and me too with harsh words, saying, the son carries the character of his mother. ॥31॥
2.1.17.32: Your father is not sinful; he follows the path of śruti and smṛti. Maheśvara, in whose feet my mind is absorbed, is my witness: ॥32॥
2.1.17.33: even after my purificatory bath following my season, I never looked here upon the face of a wicked man. Ah, how powerful is that fate by which you were born! ॥33॥
