2.1.17.34: Though instructed thus by his mother at every moment, that utterly wicked-minded one did not give up that way of life, for one given to vices is hard to teach. ॥34॥
2.1.17.35: Hunting, drink, slander, falsehood, theft, gambling, along with harlots—who in this world is not ruined by these vices? ॥35॥
2.1.17.36: Whatever he saw in the inner rooms of the house, that very wicked one would take and hand over to the gamblers—utensils of base metal, clothes and the like. ॥36॥
2.1.17.37: Once he stole his father's jewelled finger-ring that had been put away in the house, took it, and placed it in a gambler's hand. ॥37॥
2.1.17.38: By chance the priest recognised it on the hand of a gambler, and said to him: Where did you get this ring? ॥38॥
2.1.17.39: Then, questioned by him insistently again and again, he said to him: Brahmin, why do you loudly accuse me? What have I to do with theft? ॥39॥
2.1.17.40: The ring was obtained by me; it was handed over by your son himself. And indeed, the day before, a shawl was won from him and taken away for my mother. ॥40॥
2.1.17.41: Not only has this ring been handed over to me alone; to other gamblers too he has given away much wealth: ॥41॥
2.1.17.42: jewels, base metals and fine silken cloths, pitchers and the like, and various vessels made of bronze and copper. ॥42॥
2.1.17.43: Every day he is stripped naked and bound by the gamblers. There is no dice-player like him in the whole world. ॥43॥
2.1.17.44: O brahmin, how is it that until today you did not recognise your son, the crest-jewel of gamblers, expert in misconduct and bad ways? ॥44॥
2.1.17.45: Hearing this, his neck bowed low under the weight of shame, he covered his head with his cloth and entered his own house. ॥45॥
2.1.17.46: Then that dīkṣita Yajñadatta, devoted to Vedic rites, spoke to his wife, a woman of great fidelity. ॥46॥
2.1.17.47: Yajñadatta said: O wife of the dīkṣita, where is the rogue, our son Guṇanidhi? But let that be — what do I care about him? Where is that fine ring of mine, ॥47॥
2.1.17.48: which you took from my finger at the time of rubbing unguent on my body? Bring that jewelled ring quickly and give it to me. ॥48॥
2.1.17.49: Hearing his words, the dīkṣita's wife, frightened, spoke while she was performing the midday bath rites: ॥49॥
2.1.17.50: I am busy with the offerings and other tasks for the worship of the gods. This hour for guests may pass, O lover of guests. ॥50॥
2.1.17.51: Just now, busy as I was preparing cooked food, I put it somewhere in a vessel; it has slipped my mind, I do not know where. ॥51॥
2.1.17.52: The Dīkṣita said: Ha! O mother of a wicked son, ever speaker of truth, whenever I asked you, where has the son gone? — ॥52॥
2.1.17.53: each time you would say, my lord, he has just gone out with two or three friends, having studied, for further study. ॥53॥
2.1.17.54: Where is your madder-red shawl, wife, which I gave you, which always hung in the house? Tell the truth; give up fear. ॥54॥
2.1.17.55: Now that jewel-studded pitcher too is not to be seen, nor that silk triple-cloth which I gave. ॥55॥
2.1.17.56: Where is that southern bronze vessel, where that copper pot from Gauḍa? Where is that little ivory couch for pleasure and amusement? ॥56॥
2.1.17.57: Where is that statuette from the mountain country, wondrous like moonlight, graced with fingertips busy holding a lamp? ॥57॥
2.1.17.58: What use is saying more, O noble-born one? I am angry with you in vain. I shall eat only when I have married again. ॥58॥
2.1.17.59: Because of that wicked defiler of the family, I am as good as childless. Get up, bring water; I shall offer him the sesame-water oblation as for the dead. ॥59॥
2.1.17.60: For men, sonlessness is better than a bad son who disgraces the family. One should abandon one member for the sake of the family; this is the eternal rule of conduct. ॥60॥
2.1.17.61: Having bathed and performed his daily rites, on that very day the dīkṣita obtained the daughter of a certain Vedic scholar and took her hand in marriage. ॥61॥
2.1.17.iti: Thus ends the seventeenth adhyāya, named The story of Guṇanidhi, in the account of creation, in the first khaṇḍa of the second saṃhitā, the Rudra-saṃhitā, of the Śrī Śivamahāpurāṇa. ॥17॥
2.1.18.1: Brahmā said: Having heard that account in this way, and having condemned his own past conduct, the Dīkṣita's son looked toward some direction and set out. ॥1॥
2.1.18.2: Then, having gone for some time, that wicked Guṇanidhi, the son of Yajñadatta, cast out from home and with his spirit gone, stood still. ॥2॥
2.1.18.3: He fell into great anxiety: Where shall I go? What shall I do? I have not practised learning, nor am I very wealthy. ॥3॥
2.1.18.4: In a foreign land, he who has wealth quickly prospers in happiness. Yet with wealth there is fear of thieves; that obstacle arises everywhere. ॥4॥
2.1.18.5: Born in the family of a sacrificial priest—how has such great misfortune come to me? Ah, fate is indeed most powerful; it joins what is to come with past deeds. ॥5॥
2.1.18.6: I do not know how to beg; nowhere is anyone acquainted with me; and I have no money at all by my side. What refuge can there be here? ॥6॥
2.1.18.7: Always, even before the sun had risen, my mother would give me sweet food. Today, here, whom shall I beg? My mother is not here. ॥7॥
2.1.18.8: Brahmā said: While he, utterly wretched at the foot of a tree, was thinking thus over and over, O Nārada, the sun went to the western mountain. ॥8॥
2.1.18.9: At that very time a certain devotee of Maheśvara, taking offerings with him, came out of the city, ॥9॥
2.1.18.10: taking offerings of many kinds and most splendid, surrounded by his own people, having fasted on Śivarātri, in order to worship Īśāna. ॥10॥
2.1.18.11: Then that devotee, his mind attached to Śiva, entered Śiva's temple and worshipped Śaṅkara properly, with a pure heart. ॥11॥
2.1.18.12: Smelling the aroma of the cooked food, that brahmin, the son of Yajñadatta—abandoned by his father, bereft of his mother, hungry—followed him. ॥12॥
2.1.18.13: This food offered to Śiva, varied and plentiful, I shall take at night, when by luck all the Śaiva people are asleep. ॥13॥
2.1.18.14: Holding on to this hope, he sat down at the door of Śambhu, and he saw the great worship performed by that devotee. ॥14॥
2.1.18.15: When the devotees, having performed dance, song and the rest, fell asleep for a moment, he then entered Bharga's shrine to take the food-offering. ॥15॥
2.1.18.16: Seeing the lamp dim in light, in order to see the cooked food he made a wick from the hem of his own cloth and lit up the lamp, ॥16॥
2.1.18.17: then that son of Yajñadatta eagerly and hastily, with delight, seized Śiva's food-offering, plenty of cooked food, from there. ॥17॥
2.1.18.18: Then, as he was hurrying out with the cooked food, someone sleeping was woken by the blow of his foot. ॥18॥
2.1.18.19: Who is this? Who is this, rushing off? Seize him, seize him — so that man cried out in a voice loud with fear. ॥19॥
2.1.18.20: As soon as people came running together in alarm, he, fleeing, was struck down by the city-guards and in an instant passed into darkness of death. ॥20॥
2.1.18.21: And the son of Yajñadatta did not eat the offering, O sage—surely through Śiva's grace, by the power of merit that was to come. ॥21॥
2.1.18.22: When he died, he was bound by Yama's fearsome soldiers who came with nooses and maces in their hands, wishing to lead him to Saṃyamanī. ॥22॥
2.1.18.23: Just then Śiva's attendants arrived, garlanded with strings of little bells, tridents in hand, bringing a celestial chariot to take him away. ॥23॥
2.1.18.24: The attendants of Śiva said: Release this brahmin, O attendants of Yama; he is supremely righteous. This brahmin does not deserve punishment; his whole accumulation of sins is burnt away. ॥24॥
2.1.18.25: Hearing these words, Yama's attendants were greatly alarmed, and then they spoke to Mahādeva's attendants. ॥25॥
2.1.18.26: Seeing Śambhu's attendants, Yama's servants, frightened and bowing, said thus: O attendants, this brahmin is of evil conduct. ॥26॥
2.1.18.27: The attendants of Yama said: He has transgressed the custom of his family, turned away from his parents' words, fallen from truthfulness and purity, and abandoned the twilight rites and bathing. ॥27॥
2.1.18.28: Let his other deeds stay aside; he has violated what was offered to Śiva. See it here before your eyes: he is not fit to be touched by such as you. ॥28॥
2.1.18.29: Those who eat Śiva's offerings, who violate Śiva's offerings, who give away Śiva's offerings—contact with them indeed brings demerit. ॥29॥
2.1.18.30: Better to drink poison knowingly, or even to touch it is far better; but Śiva's property must not be enjoyed, even when one's life is at the throat. ॥30॥
2.1.18.31: You are the authority in matters of dharma, as we are not. If he has even a trace of merit, O attendants, we would hear it. ॥31॥
2.1.18.32: Hearing these words of Yama's servants, Śiva's servants, the attendants, remembered the lotus feet of Śiva and spoke to them. ॥32॥
2.1.18.33: The servants of Śiva said: O servants, the dharmas of Śiva are subtle; how can they be perceived by such as you, whose aim is gross? They are perceptible to those of subtle vision. ॥33॥
2.1.18.34: Hear attentively now, O attendants, the deed that was done by this sinless son of Yajñadatta. ॥34॥
2.1.18.35: The shadow of the lamp falling on the top of the liṅga was dispelled by him, as he supplied a lamp-wick from the hem of his own cloth at night. ॥35॥
2.1.18.36: Another supreme merit also arose for him there, O servants: he heard the names of Śiva, even if incidentally. Let that be taken into account. ॥36॥
2.1.18.37: The worship being performed according to rule by the devotee was watched by him, fasting on the fourteenth night, with a steady mind. ॥37॥
2.1.18.38: Today he will go to Śiva's world together with us; as a follower of Śiva he will enjoy great pleasures for some time. ॥38॥
2.1.18.39: Then, his impurities shaken off, he will become king of Kaliṅga, for this excellent brahmin is surely very dear to Śiva. ॥39॥
2.1.18.40: Nothing more need be said. You, Yama's messengers, go back to your own world as you came, with a well-pleased mind. ॥40॥
2.1.18.41: Brahmā said: O lord of sages, having heard their words, Yama's messengers all turned away and went back to Yama's world the way they had come. ॥41॥
2.1.18.42: O sage, the attendants reported everything to Yama: that whole event from the beginning, and what had been said by Śambhu's messengers in accordance with dharma. ॥42॥
2.1.18.43: Yama said: All of you attendants, listen attentively to my words, and do exactly that gladly, keeping my command foremost. ॥43॥
2.1.18.44: O attendants, those in the world who bear the tripuṇḍra mark with white ash — all of them are to be left alone; they are never to be brought here. ॥44॥
2.1.18.45: O attendants, those who smear their bodies with white ash — all of them are to be left alone; they are never to be brought here. ॥45॥
2.1.18.46: Those who in the world wear Śiva's garb for whatever reason — all of them are to be left alone; they are never to be brought here. ॥46॥
2.1.18.47: Those in the world who wear rudrākṣa beads, and those who wear matted locks — all of them are to be left alone; they are never to be brought here. ॥47॥
2.1.18.48: And those who wear Śiva's garb merely to earn a livelihood — all of them are to be left alone; they are never to be brought here. ॥48॥
2.1.18.49: Those who wear Śiva's garb even out of hypocrisy or deceit — all of them are to be left alone; they are never to be brought here. ॥49॥
2.1.18.50: Thus Yama commanded his own servants. Accepting it and saying, so be it, they all remained silent, smiling pure smiles. ॥50॥
2.1.18.51: Brahmā said: Thus freed from Yama's messengers by Śiva's attendants, that brāhmaṇa, pure in mind, quickly went with those attendants to Śiva's world. ॥51॥
2.1.18.52: There, having enjoyed all pleasures and having served Śiva and Śivā, he was reborn and became the son of Arindama, lord of Kaliṅga. ॥52॥
2.1.18.53: He was named Dama and was devoted to the service of Śiva. Even as a boy, together with other children, he practised devotion to Śiva. ॥53॥
2.1.18.54: In due course, when his father died, the young man obtained the kingdom, and gladly promoted the observances of Śiva everywhere. ॥54॥
2.1.18.55: O brāhmaṇa, that king Dama, hard to subdue, knew no other dharma except the offering of lamps in all the temples of Śiva. ॥55॥
2.1.18.56: Having summoned all the village headmen living in his realm, he commanded thus: Lamps must be offered in the temple of Śiva. ॥56॥
2.1.18.57: Otherwise — this is certainly true — he will be punished by me. Śiva becomes pleased by the offering of lamps: so the Veda declares. ॥57॥
2.1.18.58: However many Śiva temples there are around each one's village, in each of them a lamp must always be lit without hesitation. ॥58॥
2.1.18.59: For the offence of breaking my command I will cut off the offender's head, without doubt. Thus, out of fear of him, lamps were lit in every Śiva temple. ॥59॥
2.1.18.60: By this very dharma, practised as long as he lived, King Dama attained great prosperity in dharma and then came under the sway of death. ॥60॥
2.1.18.61: Because of his attachment to lamps, having lit many lamps, he became the lord of Alakā, dwelling amid the flames of jewel-lamps. ॥61॥
2.1.18.62: Thus whatever is done for Śiva, even something small, bears fruit in time. Knowing this, those who seek true happiness should worship Śiva. ॥62॥
2.1.18.63: Where was that heir of the Dīkṣita, ever averse to all dharma, who by the play of fate went to a Śiva temple to steal wealth, and who, for his own purpose, dispelled the darkness over the top of the liṅga with the light of a lamp's wick; ॥63॥
2.1.18.64: and who then obtained kingship in the land of Kaliṅga and constant delight in dharma, lighting lamps in Śiva temples because his former impressions awakened. ॥64॥
2.1.18.65: And where is this rank of a guardian of a quarter? Behold, O lord of sages, which is now enjoyed here by this one who bore a human nature. ॥65॥
2.1.18.66: Thus has been told the story of Guṇanidhi, the son of Yajñadatta, which pleases Śiva and grants all desires to those who hear it. ॥66॥
2.1.18.67: And how he came to friendship with Śiva, the God of all — listen to that too with a focused mind, dear one; I shall tell you. ॥67॥
2.1.18.iti: Thus ends the eighteenth adhyāya, named The attainment of a good end by Guṇanidhi, in the account of the going to Kailāsa within the account of creation, in the first khaṇḍa of the second saṃhitā, the Rudra-saṃhitā, of the Śrī Śivamahāpurāṇa. ॥18॥
2.1.19.1: Brahmā said: Formerly, in the Pādma kalpa, Viśravas was born from Pulastya, the mind-born son of me, Brahmā; his son was Vaiśravaṇa. ॥1॥
2.1.19.2: By him this city Alakā, built by Viśvakarman, was enjoyed, after he had formerly propitiated the god Tryambaka with extremely fierce austerity. ॥2॥
2.1.19.3: When that kalpa had passed and the Meghavāhana kalpa had begun, this glorious son of Yajñadatta performed austerity very hard to endure. ॥3॥
2.1.19.4: Having understood the power of devotion to Śambhu merely through that offering of a lamp, and having formerly reached Kāśī of Purāri, which illumines consciousness, ॥4॥
2.1.19.5: having kindled the eleven forms of Śiva with lamps that were the jewels of his mind, rich with the oil of exclusive devotion, absorbed in him, motionless in meditation, ॥5॥
2.1.19.6: using oneness with Śiva as the great vessel, intensified by the fire of austerity, free from the assault of moths—the great obstacles of desire and anger— ॥6॥
2.1.19.7: windless through restraint of breath, pure through pure vision—having installed Śambhu's liṅga, worshipped with flowers of sincere feeling, ॥7॥
2.1.19.8: he performed austerity until that body of his was reduced to skin and bone, for a hundred times ten thousand years. ॥8॥
2.1.19.9: Then the god Viśveśvara himself, together with the wide-eyed Goddess, looking upon the lord of Alakā with a gracious heart, ॥9॥
2.1.19.10: at him standing with mind fixed on the liṅga, like a motionless post, said: I am the giver of boons; so speak, O lord of Alakā. ॥10॥
2.1.19.11: As soon as the ascetic opened his eyes and looked, he saw one whose brilliance exceeded a thousand rising suns— ॥11॥
2.1.19.12: he saw before him Śrīkaṇṭha, the moon-crested lord of Umā. His eyesight overpowered by that radiance, he closed his eyes, ॥12॥
2.1.19.13: and said to the Lord of the god of gods, who is beyond the reach of the mind's desires: O Lord, grant me the power of sight to behold your feet. ॥13॥
2.1.19.14: This alone is the boon, O Lord, that you are seen directly. What need of another boon, O Īśa? Salutation to you, O moon-crested one. ॥14॥
2.1.19.15: Hearing these words of his, Umā's lord, the god of gods, touched him with his palm and gave him the power of sight. ॥15॥
2.1.19.16: Opening wide his eyes, he first looked at Umā alone. Then this son of Yajñadatta, having gained that power, thought: ॥16॥
2.1.19.17: Who is this woman beside Śambhu, beautiful in every limb? What austerity has she performed, greater even than mine? ॥17॥
2.1.19.18: Ah, what beauty! Ah, what love! Ah, what good fortune and splendour, exceedingly! So this son spoke again and again, intensely. ॥18॥
2.1.19.19: As he kept staring with an unkind gaze, repeating this again and again, his left eye burst from looking at the lovely lady. ॥19॥
2.1.19.20: Then the Goddess said to the god: What is this wicked ascetic saying, looking at me again and again? Tell me the power of his austerity. ॥20॥
2.1.19.21: Again and again, with his right eye, he looks at me alone, envious of my wealth of beauty, love and good fortune. ॥21॥
2.1.19.22: Hearing the Goddess's words, the Lord laughed and said to her: Umā, this is your son; he does not, with a cruel eye, ॥22॥
2.1.19.23: look at you; rather he would extol the splendour of your austerity. Having thus addressed the Goddess, the Lord spoke to him again: ॥23॥
2.1.19.24: I give you boons, child, pleased by this austerity. Be the master of the treasures and lord of the Guhyakas. ॥24॥
2.1.19.25: Be king of the Yakṣas and Kinnaras, king of kings, O you of good vows, lord of the Puṇyajanas, and giver of wealth to all. ॥25॥
2.1.19.26: You shall have constant friendship with me, and I shall dwell near you, close to Alakā, O friend, to increase your joy. ॥26॥
2.1.19.27: Come, fall at her feet, for she is your mother, O son of Yajñadatta, great devotee, with a fully gladdened heart. ॥27॥
2.1.19.28: Brahmā said: Having given these boons, god Śiva again spoke to Śivā: O Queen of the gods, show favour here to this ascetic, your son. ॥28॥
2.1.19.29: Hearing Śambhu's words, Pārvatī, Mother of the world, spoke to that son of Yajñadatta with a fully gladdened heart. ॥29॥
2.1.19.30: The Goddess said: Child, may your pure devotion to Bhava last forever. Be one-eyed-tawny (Ekapiṅga) by your burst left eye. ॥30॥
2.1.19.31: May the boons the god has given you be just so. Be Kubera by name, son, on account of your envy of my beauty. ॥31॥
2.1.19.32: Having thus given boons to Dhanada, the god Maheśvara, together with the Goddess, then entered the abode called Vaiśveśvara. ॥32॥
2.1.19.33: In this way Dhanada attained friendship with the glorious Śambhu, and near the city of Alakā stood Kailāsa, the abode of Śaṅkara. ॥33॥
2.1.19.iti: Thus ends the nineteenth adhyāya, named Kubera's friendship with Śiva, in the account of the going to Kailāsa, in the first khaṇḍa of the second saṃhitā, the Rudra-saṃhitā, of the Śrī Śivamahāpurāṇa. ॥19॥
2.1.20.1: Brahmā said: O Nārada, O sage, listen to the account of Śiva's excellent coming to Kailāsa, the best of mountains, brought about by the power of Kubera's penance. ॥1॥
2.1.20.2: Having granted Kubera the boon of lordship over the treasures and having gone to his own excellent abode, the Lord of the universe, the bestower of boons on Kubera, reflected in his heart: ॥2॥
2.1.20.3: Rudra, born from the body of Vidhi (Brahmā), is my own complete form, the one who performs the work of dissolution. In that form I shall go to Kailāsa, the abode of the Guhyakas. ॥3॥
2.1.20.4: Rudra, born of my heart, is indeed my complete portion, the partless Brahman, to be worshipped by Hari, Brahmā and others, not different from me, stainless. ॥4॥
2.1.20.5: In that form, becoming Kubera's friend, I, the sportive one, shall dwell right there and shall perform great penance. ॥5॥
2.1.20.6: Having thus reflected on Śiva's wish, that Rudra, eager to go, sounded there his own drum (ḍhakkā), of auspicious movement, whose very form is sound. ॥6॥
2.1.20.7: Its sound pervaded the three worlds, rousing enthusiasm, carrying the force of a summons, wondrous and densely resonant. ॥7॥
2.1.20.8: Hearing that, the gods headed by Viṣṇu and Brahmā, and likewise the sages, the Āgamas and Nigamas in embodied form, and the Siddhas went there. ॥8॥
2.1.20.9: All the gods, demons and others went there joyfully; all the Pramathas too went, wherever they had been stationed. ॥9॥
2.1.20.10: And so did the illustrious leaders of the Gaṇas, revered by all the worlds. I shall tell their number; listen attentively. ॥10॥
2.1.20.11: The Gaṇa-lord Śaṅkhakarṇa came with a crore of Gaṇas; Kekarākṣa with ten crores, and Vikṛta with eight. ॥11॥
2.1.20.12: Viśākha with sixty-four, Pāriyātraka with nine, the glorious Sarvāntaka with six, and Dundubha with eight. ॥12॥
2.1.20.13: Jālaṅka, the foremost of Gaṇas, with twelve crores; the glorious Samada with seven, and likewise Vikṛtānana. ॥13॥
2.1.20.14: Kapālī with five, the auspicious Sandāraka with six, and here Kaṇḍuka and Kuṇḍaka with crores upon crores. ॥14॥
2.1.20.15: Viṣṭambha came with eight, and Candratāpana with eight. ॥15॥
2.1.20.16: The Gaṇa-lord Mahākeśa came, surrounded by a thousand crores. ॥16॥
2.1.20.17: Kuṇḍī with twelve, likewise Vāha and the auspicious Parvataka; Kāla, Kālaka and Mahākāla with a hundred. ॥17॥
2.1.20.18: Agnika with a hundred crores, Abhimukha with a crore, Ādityamūrdhā with a crore, and likewise Dhanāvaha. ॥18॥
2.1.20.19: Sannāha with a hundred, Kumuda likewise with crores; Amogha, Kokila and Sumantraka with crores of crores. ॥19॥
2.1.20.20: Another, Kākapāda, with sixty; lord Santānaka with sixty; Mahābala with nine, and Madhupiṅga and Piṅgala. ॥20॥
2.1.20.21: Nīla with ninety came to the Lord of gods, and likewise Pūrṇabhadra; and the mighty Caturvaktra with seven crores. ॥21॥
2.1.20.22: Surrounded by twenty hundreds of thousands of crores of crores, the lord of all Gaṇas came there for the journey to Kailāsa. ॥22॥
2.1.20.23: Kāṣṭhāgūḍha with sixty-four, likewise Sukeśa and Vṛṣabha; Caitra with seven crores, and Nakulīśa, the lord himself. ॥23॥
2.1.20.24: Lokāntaka, of radiant self, and likewise lord Daityāntaka; the divine Bhṛṅgī, the glorious Riṭi, and Devadevapriya. ॥24॥
2.1.20.25: Aśani and Bhānuka, and Sanātana with sixty-four; and Nandīśvara, the mighty overlord of the Gaṇas, with a hundred crores. ॥25॥
2.1.20.26: These and other mighty Gaṇa-leaders, countless—all thousand-armed and bearing crowns of matted hair— ॥26॥
2.1.20.27: all with the moon as crest-ornament, blue-throated, three-eyed, adorned with necklaces, earrings, armlets, crowns and the like, ॥27॥
2.1.20.28: resembling Brahmā, Indra and Viṣṇu, attended by the hosts of powers such as aṇimā, shining like ten million suns—these Gaṇa-lords came there. ॥28॥
2.1.20.29: These and other great-souled Gaṇa-chiefs of spotless splendour went there with great delight, longing to see Śiva. ॥29॥
2.1.20.30: Having gone there and seen Śiva, they bowed and offered supreme praise—all of them, headed by Viṣṇu, with joined palms and bowed heads. ॥30॥
2.1.20.31: Thus, together with Viṣṇu and the others, Maheśa, the supreme Lord, went to Kailāsa out of affection for the great-souled Kubera. ॥31॥
2.1.20.32: Kubera too, together with his retinue, worshipped Śambhu who had arrived, reverently, with devotion and with various offerings. ॥32॥
2.1.20.33: Then he also duly honoured the gods headed by Viṣṇu and the other Gaṇas, the followers of Śiva, in order to please Śiva. ॥33॥
2.1.20.34: Then Śambhu, delighted at heart, embraced Kubera and, smelling his head affectionately, stayed near Alakā with all his followers. ॥34॥
2.1.20.35: The Lord commanded Viśvakarman to build on the mountain dwellings for his various devotees, as befitting his own and others. ॥35॥
2.1.20.36: Then Viśvakarman, O sage, went there and swiftly constructed works of many kinds at Śambhu's command. ॥36॥
2.1.20.37: Then Śambhu, delighted, at the request of Hari, ॥37॥
2.1.20.38: having bestowed his grace on Kubera, went to Mount Kailāsa. At an auspicious moment that supreme Lord entered his own abode, ॥38॥
2.1.20.39: and he, affectionate to his devotees, lovingly made all of them protected. Then all the gods headed by Viṣṇu, delighted, and the sages and other Siddhas joyfully consecrated Śiva. ॥39॥
2.1.20.40: All of them, with various gifts in their hands, worshipped him in turn, and performed the waving of lights (nīrājana) accompanied by a great festival. ॥40॥
2.1.20.41: Then, O sage, there was a shower of flowers, the abode of auspiciousness; and the celestial nymphs, greatly delighted and intent on singing, danced there. ॥41॥
2.1.20.42: Cries of victory and salutation, uttered by all, arose there. Then there was a great festivity that increased everyone's happiness. ॥42॥
2.1.20.43: Seated on the throne, Śambhu then shone all the more, constantly attended by all, by Viṣṇu and the others, as was fitting. ॥43॥
2.1.20.44: Then all the gods and others praised him, Śaṅkara, the benefactor of the worlds, each separately, with meaningful and pleasing words. ॥44॥
2.1.20.45: Hearing the praise, Śiva, pleased at heart, the Lord of all, the master, lovingly granted them their desires, the boons longed for in their minds. ॥45॥
2.1.20.46: Then, O sage, at Śiva's command, all of them, their desires fulfilled and delighted, went each to his own abode; and I too stayed with Viṣṇu. ॥46॥
2.1.20.47: Having seated Viṣṇu and me on a seat, Śambhu, the supreme Lord, addressing us at length and blessing us with great affection, spoke. ॥47॥
2.1.20.48: Śiva said: O Hari, O Vidhi (Brahmā), dear ones, you two are most beloved to me, the best of gods, ever the protector and creator of the three worlds. ॥48॥
2.1.20.49: Go fearlessly to your own abodes at my command, forever. I am indeed the giver of happiness to you both, and always especially watch over you. ॥49॥
2.1.20.50: Hearing these words of Śambhu, bowing deeply, at his command Hari and I went to our own abodes, gladdened in mind. ॥50॥
2.1.20.51: Right then the greatly pleased Śaṅkara joyfully seated the lord of treasures (Kubera), and, taking him by the hand, spoke auspicious words. ॥51॥
2.1.20.52: Won over by your love, friend, I have entered into friendship with you. Go fearlessly to your own place; I am always your helper, O sinless one. ॥52॥
2.1.20.53: Hearing these words of Śambhu, Kubera, gladdened in mind and full of joy, went to his own abode at his command. ॥53॥
2.1.20.54: That Śambhu dwelt on Mount Kailāsa, the best of mountains, with his attendants, devoted to yoga, free, and intent on meditation. ॥54॥
2.1.20.55: At times he meditated on his own Self; at times he was absorbed in yoga; with a free mind he lovingly narrated ancient tales to the gaṇas. ॥55॥
2.1.20.56: At times Maheśvara, skilled in sport, joyfully roamed with the gaṇas in the various lovely spots of Mount Kailāsa. ॥56॥
2.1.20.57: Thus that Śaṅkara, the supreme Lord in the form of Rudra, though the foremost of yogins, performed various sports on his own mountain. ॥57॥
2.1.20.58: Having spent some time without a wife, the supreme Lord afterwards obtained his own wife, born of Dakṣa's wife. ॥58॥
2.1.20.59: Maheśvara sported with her, Satī, the daughter of Dakṣa, and became happy, O divine sage, devoted to worldly conduct. ॥59॥
2.1.20.60: Thus, O lord of sages, this incarnation of Rudra has been described to you, and his coming to Kailāsa, and indeed his friendship with the lord of treasures. ॥60॥
2.1.20.61: The sport contained within it has also been described, which increases knowledge and which always grants the fruit of all desires here and hereafter. ॥61॥
2.1.20.62: Whoever reads this story or listens to it attentively attains enjoyment here and obtains liberation in the next world. ॥62॥
2.1.20.iti: Thus ends the twentieth adhyāya, named Śiva goes to Kailāsa, in the account of Kailāsa within the account of creation, in the first khaṇḍa of the second saṃhitā, the Rudra-saṃhitā, of the Śrī Śivamahāpurāṇa. ॥20॥
